\"<h2>中文教学指南：十五岁学生<\/h2><p><strong>简明翻译版。<\/strong>本版介绍主要课程顺序、概念和评估，并非下方完整英语工作表及评分描述的逐项翻译。<\/p><h3>目标与成果<\/h3><p>探究树枝特征与其表现之间的关系。学生应能描述至少四项特征；使用适当单位测量长度、直径和质量；提出可检验假设；识别变量；实施教师批准的探究；作图；说明两项局限及相应改进。暂以英格兰第四关键阶段科学探究要求为参考，实施时须对照本校实际课程。<\/p><h3>准备与安全<\/h3><p>准备已编号和检查的试样、尺、天平、可用的卡尺、稳定支架及记录表。剔除尖锐、开裂起刺或发霉试样。教师须预先测试跨距和小载荷，使弯曲可测且不造成损坏。不得以折断为目标。手和脸应远离试验区；发现开裂声、滑动或永久变形时立即停止。使用预先收集的材料，避免破坏栖息地。<\/p><h3>第一课：观察与比较，六十分钟<\/h3><p>0–8分钟：描述两根树枝并预测表现。8–16分钟：区分观察与推断，介绍词汇。16–25分钟：示范测量、单位和精度。25–45分钟：检查至少四个试样，轮换测量、记录、器材和核查角色。45–55分钟：比较结果并提出可检验问题。55–60分钟：提交一项观察、一项推断及一项带单位的测量。<\/p><h3>第二课：预测与计划，六十分钟<\/h3><p>核心问题：固定载荷下，直径与弯曲有何关系？将位移定义为中点相对无载位置的垂直移动。确定编号、直径测量位置、跨距、总载荷、加载位置、试样方向、读数时间及重复次数。互评后获得教师批准。树种、含水量、节疤和状态可能混杂比较。重复读取同一试样不等于增加独立试样。<\/p><h3>第三课：探究与分析，六十分钟<\/h3><p>按批准方案记录加载与无载读数并求差。卸载后检查是否恢复，再重复。保持约定条件一致。对有效读数求平均，以直径为横轴、平均位移为纵轴绘制散点图，标注单位并采用均匀刻度。不要按试样顺序连点，也不要仅因结果不符合预测而删除它。若时间不足，应先试行工作量，再减少样本或另设作图时间。<\/p><h3>第四课：评价与应用，六十分钟<\/h3><p>判断证据是否支持假设，引用至少两项结果，说明两项局限及各自改进。为教师指定跨距的小型模型桥构件推荐试样，附示意图，并提出接头、结构布局、重复加载和破坏强度等后续试验。推荐不等于已证明承载能力或桥梁安全。<\/p><h3>核心工作表<\/h3><p>观察记录：试样、长度、直径、质量、纹理、状态和观察。计划：问题、假设、比较变量、测量结果、控制条件、方法、无法控制的因素、停止条件和批准。结果表：试样、直径（毫米）、三次位移（毫米）及平均值；另记跨距、总载荷和读数时间。<\/p><p>平均值＝有效位移读数之和÷有效次数。仅作模拟示例：(4＋5＋3)÷3＝4毫米。不能把模拟数字当作实验结果。在可比条件下弯曲较少，说明该装置下抗弯更强，并不证明断裂载荷更高。<\/p><h3>推理活动<\/h3><p>将陈述分为观察、推断和预测。例如“天平显示24克”是观察；“它可能含水更多”是推断；“相同载荷下它会弯曲更少”是预测。审查一个对粗细树枝使用不同跨距和载荷的错误计划，修正控制条件、读数次数和抽样，并纠正“弯曲最少就总是最结实”的结论。<\/p><h3>评估与答案<\/h3><p>个人成果应包括问题与假设、方法和变量、结果表与图、引用数据的结论、两项局限及改进、以及有依据的建议。可以共享小组数据，但解释必须独立。等效录音展示应保持相同科学要求。<\/p><p>另设十分知识检查：测量结果与单位2分；两个控制条件2分；3、4、5毫米平均值1分；重复与独立试样的区别2分；弯曲与破坏的区别1分；局限及相应改进2分。答案要点：中点垂直位移，毫米等长度单位；跨距和总载荷等控制条件；平均4毫米；重复反映一致性，独立试样反映试样间差异；未测断裂载荷。<\/p><p>探究量规共十五分，五个标准各0–3分：观察与测量、计划、分析、结论与应用、评价。0分表示无相关证据；1分为不完整或不一致；2分为清楚且大体正确；3分为准确、有论证且明确局限，具体以原始描述为准。十五分探究与十分检查分开报告，不能把总分当作经验证的GCSE等级界线。<\/p><h3>支持、人工智能与教学评价<\/h3><p>提供图示词汇、例题、引导表格、建议坐标刻度及适当口头回答方式。拓展可涉及仪器分辨率、变异和控制混杂因素的更强设计。教师可用人工智能起草资料和明确标注的错误示例，但必须核查；学生无需人工智能账户。不要上传可识别个人的作业。实施后查看起始与结束回答、作品、参与、时间和无障碍表现。目前尚未测得学习成效或备课时间节省。<\/p>\", \"<h2>中文教学指南：大学一年级<\/h2><p><strong>简明翻译版。<\/strong>保留核心概念、课程顺序、数值示例和评估标准。下方保留完整英语原版。<\/p><h3>目标与准备<\/h3><p>通过力—位移测量、分析和有限推断，探究树枝作为天然结构材料的表现。假定具备基础代数、国际单位制和作图能力；专门理论在课程中介绍。安排四次两小时课程，另加约六小时自主学习。先检查单位换算、斜率及刚度与破坏强度的区别。试验前，教师必须批准装置、步骤、载荷限制和停止条件。<\/p><h3>模型与局限<\/h3><p>理想中央加载三点弯曲模型：δ＝FL³/(48EI)；k＝dF/dδ；圆截面I＝πd⁴/64；E_app＝kL³/(48I)。区分试样及装置刚度k、材料模量E、抗弯刚度EI和破坏强度。E_app依赖几何、支承、材料和小变形假设；条件不足时仅报告k。锥度、椭圆截面、各向异性、含水量和节疤不能简单当作随机测量噪声。<\/p><h3>第一次课程：表征与理论<\/h3><p>0–15分钟诊断；15–35分钟介绍模型及SI计算；35–70分钟编号并记录质量、长度，以及三个位置各两个垂直方向直径、状态和方向；70–85分钟休息并整理几何；85–105分钟比较试样和假设，区分测量不确定度与生物变异；105–120分钟批判“越粗总是越强”，提交问题和抽样理由。<\/p><h3>第二次课程：方案与试验<\/h3><p>0–15分钟复核假设；15–35分钟审查缺陷方案；35–60分钟设计固定跨距的加载卸载、读数时间和可追溯记录；60–70分钟休息及教师审核；70–100分钟在批准范围内试验，检查分辨率、重复性及恢复；100–120分钟修订方案、分析与排除标准。明确控制条件、独立试样和技术重复。同一试样十个循环不等于十个独立试样。<\/p><h3>第三次课程：测量与分析<\/h3><p>0–10分钟确认设备与限制；10–50分钟采集独立试样数据并适当重复；50–60分钟检查数据完整性；60–85分钟用SI绘制F对δ图，对合理线性范围进行含截距拟合，检查残差及加载卸载差异；85–105分钟估计k及有依据的E_app，分开讨论测量敏感性和试样差异；105–120分钟互评并写有限结论。不得无理由强制零截距，不应隐藏滞回、漂移或残余变形。<\/p><h3>第四次课程：批判与应用<\/h3><p>0–20分钟展示图及局限；20–40分钟核查对照结论的证据与假设；40–65分钟结合刚度、质量和不确定度推荐模型桥构件；65–75分钟休息并准备报告结构；75–100分钟互评；100–115分钟个人口头检查或获批等效形式；115–120分钟提交修改重点和人工智能声明。不能由本试验推断整桥安全或断裂载荷。<\/p><h3>记录与模拟算例<\/h3><p>保留试样和循环编号、添加质量、力、位移、加载或卸载及时间。另记仪器分辨率、零点、附件质量、方向、偏离方案和修正。保留原始数据并说明小组贡献。<\/p><p>单个理想试样的模拟数据：力为0、1、2、3、4牛，位移为0、0.20、0.40、0.60、0.80毫米。L＝0.200米，d＝0.0060米。结果：k＝5牛/毫米＝5000牛/米；I≈6.36×10⁻¹¹米⁴；E_app≈1.31×10¹⁰帕＝13.1吉帕。这些是构造数据，不是实验观察或独立重复。完美直线不能估计真实噪声，也不能验证物理模型。<\/p><h3>不确定度与批判判断<\/h3><p>在圆截面模型、小且相互独立的标准不确定度条件下：u(E)/E≈√[(u(k)/k)²＋(3u(L)/L)²＋(4u(d)/d)²]。直径2%的不确定度单独贡献约8%的模量相对不确定度。此传播式不包含模型偏差、锥度、各向异性或未知含水量。高R²不能验证物理假设，也不能证明破坏强度。<\/p><p>理想模型中，其他量不变时跨距加倍使位移增至八倍；圆直径加倍使位移降至十六分之一。应解释真实树枝何时不满足这些预测。审查改变控制条件、独立抽样不足、伪重复和无依据推断。<\/p><h3>评估<\/h3><p>个人报告1500字，不含参考文献、表格和附录，建议占单元90%。报告内标准：问题与物理推理15%；设计与可重复性20%；数据分析25%；不确定度与批判评价25%；沟通与诚信15%。提交原始数据、可检查公式或代码、共享数据来源及帮助声明。口头检查建议占10%：解释一个计算、论证一个决策、指出一个改变解释的局限；物理推理、数据解释和批判判断等权。须采用本校评分尺度与规定。<\/p><h3>支持、人工智能与修订<\/h3><p>提供引导电子表格、换算例题和模板，同时提供开放分析路径。拓展关注几何敏感性、不确定度传播或不同模型。因无法实践而使用模拟数据时，实践能力仍需另行取证。 \"<h2>中文教学指南：十五岁学生<\/h2><p><strong>简明翻译版。<\/strong>本版介绍主要课程顺序、概念和评估，并非下方完整英语工作表及评分描述的逐项翻译。<\/p><h3>目标与成果<\/h3><p>探究树枝特征与其表现之间的关系。学生应能描述至少四项特征；使用适当单位测量长度、直径和质量；提出可检验假设；识别变量；实施教师批准的探究；作图；说明两项局限及相应改进。暂以英格兰第四关键阶段科学探究要求为参考，实施时须对照本校实际课程。<\/p><h3>准备与安全<\/h3><p>准备已编号和检查的试样、尺、天平、可用的卡尺、稳定支架及记录表。剔除尖锐、开裂起刺或发霉试样。教师须预先测试跨距和小载荷，使弯曲可测且不造成损坏。不得以折断为目标。手和脸应远离试验区；发现开裂声、滑动或永久变形时立即停止。使用预先收集的材料，避免破坏栖息地。<\/p><h3>第一课：观察与比较，六十分钟<\/h3><p>0–8分钟：描述两根树枝并预测表现。8–16分钟：区分观察与推断，介绍词汇。16–25分钟：示范测量、单位和精度。25–45分钟：检查至少四个试样，轮换测量、记录、器材和核查角色。45–55分钟：比较结果并提出可检验问题。55–60分钟：提交一项观察、一项推断及一项带单位的测量。<\/p><h3>第二课：预测与计划，六十分钟<\/h3><p>核心问题：固定载荷下，直径与弯曲有何关系？将位移定义为中点相对无载位置的垂直移动。确定编号、直径测量位置、跨距、总载荷、加载位置、试样方向、读数时间及重复次数。互评后获得教师批准。树种、含水量、节疤和状态可能混杂比较。重复读取同一试样不等于增加独立试样。<\/p><h3>第三课：探究与分析，六十分钟<\/h3><p>按批准方案记录加载与无载读数并求差。卸载后检查是否恢复，再重复。保持约定条件一致。对有效读数求平均，以直径为横轴、平均位移为纵轴绘制散点图，标注单位并采用均匀刻度。不要按试样顺序连点，也不要仅因结果不符合预测而删除它。若时间不足，应先试行工作量，再减少样本或另设作图时间。<\/p><h3>第四课：评价与应用，六十分钟<\/h3><p>判断证据是否支持假设，引用至少两项结果，说明两项局限及各自改进。为教师指定跨距的小型模型桥构件推荐试样，附示意图，并提出接头、结构布局、重复加载和破坏强度等后续试验。推荐不等于已证明承载能力或桥梁安全。<\/p><h3>核心工作表<\/h3><p>观察记录：试样、长度、直径、质量、纹理、状态和观察。计划：问题、假设、比较变量、测量结果、控制条件、方法、无法控制的因素、停止条件和批准。结果表：试样、直径（毫米）、三次位移（毫米）及平均值；另记跨距、总载荷和读数时间。<\/p><p>平均值＝有效位移读数之和÷有效次数。仅作模拟示例：(4＋5＋3)÷3＝4毫米。不能把模拟数字当作实验结果。在可比条件下弯曲较少，说明该装置下抗弯更强，并不证明断裂载荷更高。<\/p><h3>推理活动<\/h3><p>将陈述分为观察、推断和预测。例如“天平显示24克”是观察；“它可能含水更多”是推断；“相同载荷下它会弯曲更少”是预测。审查一个对粗细树枝使用不同跨距和载荷的错误计划，修正控制条件、读数次数和抽样，并纠正“弯曲最少就总是最结实”的结论。<\/p><h3>评估与答案<\/h3><p>个人成果应包括问题与假设、方法和变量、结果表与图、引用数据的结论、两项局限及改进、以及有依据的建议。可以共享小组数据，但解释必须独立。等效录音展示应保持相同科学要求。<\/p><p>另设十分知识检查：测量结果与单位2分；两个控制条件2分；3、4、5毫米平均值1分；重复与独立试样的区别2分；弯曲与破坏的区别1分；局限及相应改进2分。答案要点：中点垂直位移，毫米等长度单位；跨距和总载荷等控制条件；平均4毫米；重复反映一致性，独立试样反映试样间差异；未测断裂载荷。<\/p><p>探究量规共十五分，五个标准各0–3分：观察与测量、计划、分析、结论与应用、评价。0分表示无相关证据；1分为不完整或不一致；2分为清楚且大体正确；3分为准确、有论证且明确局限，具体以原始描述为准。十五分探究与十分检查分开报告，不能把总分当作经验证的GCSE等级界线。<\/p><h3>支持、人工智能与教学评价<\/h3><p>提供图示词汇、例题、引导表格、建议坐标刻度及适当口头回答方式。拓展可涉及仪器分辨率、变异和控制混杂因素的更强设计。教师可用人工智能起草资料和明确标注的错误示例，但必须核查；学生无需人工智能账户。不要上传可识别个人的作业。实施后查看起始与结束回答、作品、参与、时间和无障碍表现。目前尚未测得学习成效或备课时间节省。<\/p>\", \"<h2>中文教学指南：大学一年级<\/h2><p><strong>简明翻译版。<\/strong>保留核心概念、课程顺序、数值示例和评估标准。下方保留完整英语原版。<\/p><h3>目标与准备<\/h3><p>通过力—位移测量、分析和有限推断，探究树枝作为天然结构材料的表现。假定具备基础代数、国际单位制和作图能力；专门理论在课程中介绍。安排四次两小时课程，另加约六小时自主学习。先检查单位换算、斜率及刚度与破坏强度的区别。试验前，教师必须批准装置、步骤、载荷限制和停止条件。<\/p><h3>模型与局限<\/h3><p>理想中央加载三点弯曲模型：δ＝FL³/(48EI)；k＝dF/dδ；圆截面I＝πd⁴/64；E_app＝kL³/(48I)。区分试样及装置刚度k、材料模量E、抗弯刚度EI和破坏强度。E_app依赖几何、支承、材料和小变形假设；条件不足时仅报告k。锥度、椭圆截面、各向异性、含水量和节疤不能简单当作随机测量噪声。<\/p><h3>第一次课程：表征与理论<\/h3><p>0–15分钟诊断；15–35分钟介绍模型及SI计算；35–70分钟编号并记录质量、长度，以及三个位置各两个垂直方向直径、状态和方向；70–85分钟休息并整理几何；85–105分钟比较试样和假设，区分测量不确定度与生物变异；105–120分钟批判“越粗总是越强”，提交问题和抽样理由。<\/p><h3>第二次课程：方案与试验<\/h3><p>0–15分钟复核假设；15–35分钟审查缺陷方案；35–60分钟设计固定跨距的加载卸载、读数时间和可追溯记录；60–70分钟休息及教师审核；70–100分钟在批准范围内试验，检查分辨率、重复性及恢复；100–120分钟修订方案、分析与排除标准。明确控制条件、独立试样和技术重复。同一试样十个循环不等于十个独立试样。<\/p><h3>第三次课程：测量与分析<\/h3><p>0–10分钟确认设备与限制；10–50分钟采集独立试样数据并适当重复；50–60分钟检查数据完整性；60–85分钟用SI绘制F对δ图，对合理线性范围进行含截距拟合，检查残差及加载卸载差异；85–105分钟估计k及有依据的E_app，分开讨论测量敏感性和试样差异；105–120分钟互评并写有限结论。不得无理由强制零截距，不应隐藏滞回、漂移或残余变形。<\/p><h3>第四次课程：批判与应用<\/h3><p>0–20分钟展示图及局限；20–40分钟核查对照结论的证据与假设；40–65分钟结合刚度、质量和不确定度推荐模型桥构件；65–75分钟休息并准备报告结构；75–100分钟互评；100–115分钟个人口头检查或获批等效形式；115–120分钟提交修改重点和人工智能声明。不能由本试验推断整桥安全或断裂载荷。<\/p><h3>记录与模拟算例<\/h3><p>保留试样和循环编号、添加质量、力、位移、加载或卸载及时间。另记仪器分辨率、零点、附件质量、方向、偏离方案和修正。保留原始数据并说明小组贡献。<\/p><p>单个理想试样的模拟数据：力为0、1、2、3、4牛，位移为0、0.20、0.40、0.60、0.80毫米。L＝0.200米，d＝0.0060米。结果：k＝5牛/毫米＝5000牛/米；I≈6.36×10⁻¹¹米⁴；E_app≈1.31×10¹⁰帕＝13.1吉帕。这些是构造数据，不是实验观察或独立重复。完美直线不能估计真实噪声，也不能验证物理模型。<\/p><h3>不确定度与批判判断<\/h3><p>在圆截面模型、小且相互独立的标准不确定度条件下：u(E)/E≈√[(u(k)/k)²＋(3u(L)/L)²＋(4u(d)/d)²]。直径2%的不确定度单独贡献约8%的模量相对不确定度。此传播式不包含模型偏差、锥度、各向异性或未知含水量。高R²不能验证物理假设，也不能证明破坏强度。<\/p><p>理想模型中，其他量不变时跨距加倍使位移增至八倍；圆直径加倍使位移降至十六分之一。应解释真实树枝何时不满足这些预测。审查改变控制条件、独立抽样不足、伪重复和无依据推断。<\/p><h3>评估<\/h3><p>个人报告1500字，不含参考文献、表格和附录，建议占单元90%。报告内标准：问题与物理推理15%；设计与可重复性20%；数据分析25%；不确定度与批判评价25%；沟通与诚信15%。提交原始数据、可检查公式或代码、共享数据来源及帮助声明。口头检查建议占10%：解释一个计算、论证一个决策、指出一个改变解释的局限；物理推理、数据解释和批判判断等权。须采用本校评分尺度与规定。<\/p><h3>支持、人工智能与修订<\/h3><p>提供引导电子表格、换算例题和模板，同时提供开放分析路径。拓展关注几何敏感性、不确定度传播或不同模型。因无法实践而使用模拟数据时，实践能力仍需另行取证。 style=\"grid-column:1/-1\" hidden><\/section><main class=\"shell\" id=\"mainContent\"><div class=\"panel\" data-panel=\"reflection\"><section class=\"card\">\n<h2 id=\"nav-section-1\">What I have learned from this starting point<\/h2>\n<p>Looking back, the most useful part of this project has been discovering how much changes when the same investigation is designed for two different audiences. Starting with sticks gave me a familiar material and a manageable way to explore the relationship between outcomes, activities, assessment and interface. It also made it easy to begin building before I had established enough about the people who would use the result. That is the central limitation of this starting point.<\/p>\n<p>This is a self-directed prototype built around a fictional brief, rather than a response to an agreed institutional need. I have made assumptions about prior knowledge, available time, apparatus, tutor support and access needs. The working pages make those assumptions visible, but they do not validate them. I can demonstrate design decisions and functioning interactions; I cannot yet demonstrate that the proposed learning journey is effective, appropriate for a particular cohort or practical to deliver.<\/p>\n<h3 id=\"reflection-stakeholders\">What I would establish with stakeholders first<\/h3>\n<p>In a live project, I would begin with the people involved: the commissioner or institutional sponsor, learners, subject specialists, tutors, assessment leads, learning support and accessibility colleagues, and the staff responsible for technology and delivery. For the school route, I would also involve the relevant safeguarding and data-protection leads and agree when parent or carer input is appropriate. I would establish the problem we are trying to solve, the evidence that it exists, the constraints and what success would look like before agreeing the solution.<\/p>\n<p>My experience with Skillkit and the Manchester Institute for Information Delivery taught me how much learner and administrator feedback can change an apparently sound design. Here, much of that dialogue has been represented by my own judgement. In practice, I would use interviews, observation, examples of current learner work and a short diagnostic task to challenge my assumptions. I would agree outcomes, assessment requirements, responsibilities and evaluation measures with stakeholders, then return to them at review points throughout the project.<\/p>\n<h3 id=\"audience-interface-reflection\">What the two learner interfaces have taught me<\/h3>\n<p>Developing the age-15 activity reminded me that a clear next action can matter as much as a good explanation. Short challenges, visible stick choices and prompts linked to the selected stick give the learner something concrete to do and explain. The undergraduate route makes more room for quantities, units, uncertainty and model assumptions, and asks the learner to take greater responsibility for interpretation. Those are provisional decisions about support and challenge, rather than conclusions about what everyone of a particular age needs.<\/p>\n<p>The repeated revisions also exposed a weakness in my process: improvements to one part of the interface sometimes disrupted another. Navigation, tables, translations and avatar behaviour needed checking together, rather than as separate finishing tasks. I would now establish shared components and acceptance criteria earlier, then test representative pages in each language and on different devices before extending a change. The playful guide and the more technical presentation both need evidence from intended users; visual appeal alone does not establish that either helps learning.<\/p>\n<h3 id=\"reflection-addie\">How I would use ADDIE in a live project<\/h3>\n<p>I would use ADDIE as a framework for enquiry and review, rather than a sequence of boxes to complete. Analysis would establish the need, audience, context and baseline evidence with stakeholders. Design would connect agreed outcomes with the learning sequence, support, assessment and evaluation plan. Development would produce small, testable examples for subject, accessibility and user review before building the complete experience.<\/p>\n<p>Implementation would include tutor preparation, approved practical arrangements, learner support, technical checks and a limited pilot in the intended setting. Evaluation would run through every stage: formative feedback would inform revisions, and the pilot would test the agreed measures of learning and usability. A finding at any stage could send me back to the analysis or design. In this project, I have explored design and development extensively, but the analysis remains provisional and implementation and evaluation in a real teaching setting have not taken place.<\/p>\n<h3 id=\"nav-section-2\">What working with AI has made me reconsider<\/h3>\n<p>AI helped me draft resources, explore alternative explanations and implement a working prototype quickly. That speed was useful, but it also made it possible to produce more material than I had adequately reviewed. I had to keep returning to the purpose of each addition and remove elements that made the experience harder to follow. My responsibility remains to question the output, check subject accuracy and accessibility, and decide whether a change serves the intended learning. This work demonstrates an iterative collaboration with AI, not independently authored code or evidence that AI improves learning.<\/p>\n<h3 id=\"nav-section-3\">What evidence I still need<\/h3>\n<p>I would want to see learners use the activities, explain their reasoning and respond to feedback. Matched entry and exit tasks, individual work assessed against agreed criteria, tutor observations and learner feedback would give a more useful picture than completion figures alone. I would also examine who struggled to participate, where instructions caused uncertainty, how long the work took and whether the practical measurements supported the intended conclusions. A small pilot could identify problems and suggest improvements; it would not, by itself, establish that the design caused better outcomes.<\/p>\n<h3 id=\"nav-section-4\">Where the project stands and what I would do now<\/h3>\n<p>We now have a working prototype with two learning pathways, teaching packs, activities and an explanation of the design decisions. That is a basis for review, not a course ready for institutional adoption. In a live project, my next step would be a structured stakeholder review against the original need, followed by a subject and assessment check, accessibility and device testing, and a supervised rehearsal of the practical work. I would prioritise any problems that prevent participation or undermine the validity of the task before adding more features.<\/p>\n<p>I would then agree a small pilot, the support and consent arrangements it requires, the evidence to collect and the criteria for deciding whether to revise, extend or stop. Tutors would need preparation and a clear route for reporting issues; ownership of content, maintenance and learner data would need to be agreed. I would use the findings to revise the learning journey and return to stakeholders for a decision about wider delivery. The next useful advance is therefore to test the assumptions with real people in a real setting, rather than continue polishing the prototype in isolation.<\/p>\n<\/section><section class=\"card\"><h3 id=\"nav-section-5\">Read the comparison document<\/h3><p>Use the full comparison to inspect the choices behind the two pathways alongside this reflection.<\/p><a class=\"action\" href=\"learning-comparison-document.html#nav-section-1\">Open comparison document<\/a><\/section><a class=\"action\" href=\"interactive-learning.html#project-entry-title\">Return to the introduction<\/a><\/div><\/main>\n<section class=\"card\" id=\"designExplanation\" style=\"grid-column:1/-1\"><\/section><footer>Jonathan Pincher · <a href=\"education.html\">Back to Education &amp; Learning Design<\/a><\/footer><\/div><script>\n(()=>{\nif(location.hostname==='jpincher.github.io'){const online=document.getElementById('onlineAccess');if(online)online.hidden=true;}const $=id=>document.getElementById(id),lang=$('guideLanguage');let saved='en';try{saved=localStorage.getItem('jp-guide-language')||'en'}catch{}if(!['en','es','zh'].includes(saved))saved='en';lang.value=saved;\nconst copy={en:{heading:'Your section guide',play:'Play introduction',stop:'Stop',note:'Navigation and introductions are available in three languages. \"<h2>中文教学指南：十五岁学生<\/h2><p><strong>简明翻译版。<\/strong>本版介绍主要课程顺序、概念和评估，并非下方完整英语工作表及评分描述的逐项翻译。<\/p><h3>目标与成果<\/h3><p>探究树枝特征与其表现之间的关系。学生应能描述至少四项特征；使用适当单位测量长度、直径和质量；提出可检验假设；识别变量；实施教师批准的探究；作图；说明两项局限及相应改进。暂以英格兰第四关键阶段科学探究要求为参考，实施时须对照本校实际课程。<\/p><h3>准备与安全<\/h3><p>准备已编号和检查的试样、尺、天平、可用的卡尺、稳定支架及记录表。剔除尖锐、开裂起刺或发霉试样。教师须预先测试跨距和小载荷，使弯曲可测且不造成损坏。不得以折断为目标。手和脸应远离试验区；发现开裂声、滑动或永久变形时立即停止。使用预先收集的材料，避免破坏栖息地。<\/p><h3>第一课：观察与比较，六十分钟<\/h3><p>0–8分钟：描述两根树枝并预测表现。8–16分钟：区分观察与推断，介绍词汇。16–25分钟：示范测量、单位和精度。25–45分钟：检查至少四个试样，轮换测量、记录、器材和核查角色。45–55分钟：比较结果并提出可检验问题。55–60分钟：提交一项观察、一项推断及一项带单位的测量。<\/p><h3>第二课：预测与计划，六十分钟<\/h3><p>核心问题：固定载荷下，直径与弯曲有何关系？将位移定义为中点相对无载位置的垂直移动。确定编号、直径测量位置、跨距、总载荷、加载位置、试样方向、读数时间及重复次数。互评后获得教师批准。树种、含水量、节疤和状态可能混杂比较。重复读取同一试样不等于增加独立试样。<\/p><h3>第三课：探究与分析，六十分钟<\/h3><p>按批准方案记录加载与无载读数并求差。卸载后检查是否恢复，再重复。保持约定条件一致。对有效读数求平均，以直径为横轴、平均位移为纵轴绘制散点图，标注单位并采用均匀刻度。不要按试样顺序连点，也不要仅因结果不符合预测而删除它。若时间不足，应先试行工作量，再减少样本或另设作图时间。<\/p><h3>第四课：评价与应用，六十分钟<\/h3><p>判断证据是否支持假设，引用至少两项结果，说明两项局限及各自改进。为教师指定跨距的小型模型桥构件推荐试样，附示意图，并提出接头、结构布局、重复加载和破坏强度等后续试验。推荐不等于已证明承载能力或桥梁安全。<\/p><h3>核心工作表<\/h3><p>观察记录：试样、长度、直径、质量、纹理、状态和观察。计划：问题、假设、比较变量、测量结果、控制条件、方法、无法控制的因素、停止条件和批准。结果表：试样、直径（毫米）、三次位移（毫米）及平均值；另记跨距、总载荷和读数时间。<\/p><p>平均值＝有效位移读数之和÷有效次数。仅作模拟示例：(4＋5＋3)÷3＝4毫米。不能把模拟数字当作实验结果。在可比条件下弯曲较少，说明该装置下抗弯更强，并不证明断裂载荷更高。<\/p><h3>推理活动<\/h3><p>将陈述分为观察、推断和预测。例如“天平显示24克”是观察；“它可能含水更多”是推断；“相同载荷下它会弯曲更少”是预测。审查一个对粗细树枝使用不同跨距和载荷的错误计划，修正控制条件、读数次数和抽样，并纠正“弯曲最少就总是最结实”的结论。<\/p><h3>评估与答案<\/h3><p>个人成果应包括问题与假设、方法和变量、结果表与图、引用数据的结论、两项局限及改进、以及有依据的建议。可以共享小组数据，但解释必须独立。等效录音展示应保持相同科学要求。<\/p><p>另设十分知识检查：测量结果与单位2分；两个控制条件2分；3、4、5毫米平均值1分；重复与独立试样的区别2分；弯曲与破坏的区别1分；局限及相应改进2分。答案要点：中点垂直位移，毫米等长度单位；跨距和总载荷等控制条件；平均4毫米；重复反映一致性，独立试样反映试样间差异；未测断裂载荷。<\/p><p>探究量规共十五分，五个标准各0–3分：观察与测量、计划、分析、结论与应用、评价。0分表示无相关证据；1分为不完整或不一致；2分为清楚且大体正确；3分为准确、有论证且明确局限，具体以原始描述为准。十五分探究与十分检查分开报告，不能把总分当作经验证的GCSE等级界线。<\/p><h3>支持、人工智能与教学评价<\/h3><p>提供图示词汇、例题、引导表格、建议坐标刻度及适当口头回答方式。拓展可涉及仪器分辨率、变异和控制混杂因素的更强设计。教师可用人工智能起草资料和明确标注的错误示例，但必须核查；学生无需人工智能账户。不要上传可识别个人的作业。实施后查看起始与结束回答、作品、参与、时间和无障碍表现。目前尚未测得学习成效或备课时间节省。<\/p>\", \"<h2>中文教学指南：大学一年级<\/h2><p><strong>简明翻译版。<\/strong>保留核心概念、课程顺序、数值示例和评估标准。下方保留完整英语原版。<\/p><h3>目标与准备<\/h3><p>通过力—位移测量、分析和有限推断，探究树枝作为天然结构材料的表现。假定具备基础代数、国际单位制和作图能力；专门理论在课程中介绍。安排四次两小时课程，另加约六小时自主学习。先检查单位换算、斜率及刚度与破坏强度的区别。试验前，教师必须批准装置、步骤、载荷限制和停止条件。<\/p><h3>模型与局限<\/h3><p>理想中央加载三点弯曲模型：δ＝FL³/(48EI)；k＝dF/dδ；圆截面I＝πd⁴/64；E_app＝kL³/(48I)。区分试样及装置刚度k、材料模量E、抗弯刚度EI和破坏强度。E_app依赖几何、支承、材料和小变形假设；条件不足时仅报告k。锥度、椭圆截面、各向异性、含水量和节疤不能简单当作随机测量噪声。<\/p><h3>第一次课程：表征与理论<\/h3><p>0–15分钟诊断；15–35分钟介绍模型及SI计算；35–70分钟编号并记录质量、长度，以及三个位置各两个垂直方向直径、状态和方向；70–85分钟休息并整理几何；85–105分钟比较试样和假设，区分测量不确定度与生物变异；105–120分钟批判“越粗总是越强”，提交问题和抽样理由。<\/p><h3>第二次课程：方案与试验<\/h3><p>0–15分钟复核假设；15–35分钟审查缺陷方案；35–60分钟设计固定跨距的加载卸载、读数时间和可追溯记录；60–70分钟休息及教师审核；70–100分钟在批准范围内试验，检查分辨率、重复性及恢复；100–120分钟修订方案、分析与排除标准。明确控制条件、独立试样和技术重复。同一试样十个循环不等于十个独立试样。<\/p><h3>第三次课程：测量与分析<\/h3><p>0–10分钟确认设备与限制；10–50分钟采集独立试样数据并适当重复；50–60分钟检查数据完整性；60–85分钟用SI绘制F对δ图，对合理线性范围进行含截距拟合，检查残差及加载卸载差异；85–105分钟估计k及有依据的E_app，分开讨论测量敏感性和试样差异；105–120分钟互评并写有限结论。不得无理由强制零截距，不应隐藏滞回、漂移或残余变形。<\/p><h3>第四次课程：批判与应用<\/h3><p>0–20分钟展示图及局限；20–40分钟核查对照结论的证据与假设；40–65分钟结合刚度、质量和不确定度推荐模型桥构件；65–75分钟休息并准备报告结构；75–100分钟互评；100–115分钟个人口头检查或获批等效形式；115–120分钟提交修改重点和人工智能声明。不能由本试验推断整桥安全或断裂载荷。<\/p><h3>记录与模拟算例<\/h3><p>保留试样和循环编号、添加质量、力、位移、加载或卸载及时间。另记仪器分辨率、零点、附件质量、方向、偏离方案和修正。保留原始数据并说明小组贡献。<\/p><p>单个理想试样的模拟数据：力为0、1、2、3、4牛，位移为0、0.20、0.40、0.60、0.80毫米。L＝0.200米，d＝0.0060米。结果：k＝5牛/毫米＝5000牛/米；I≈6.36×10⁻¹¹米⁴；E_app≈1.31×10¹⁰帕＝13.1吉帕。这些是构造数据，不是实验观察或独立重复。完美直线不能估计真实噪声，也不能验证物理模型。<\/p><h3>不确定度与批判判断<\/h3><p>在圆截面模型、小且相互独立的标准不确定度条件下：u(E)/E≈√[(u(k)/k)²＋(3u(L)/L)²＋(4u(d)/d)²]。直径2%的不确定度单独贡献约8%的模量相对不确定度。此传播式不包含模型偏差、锥度、各向异性或未知含水量。高R²不能验证物理假设，也不能证明破坏强度。<\/p><p>理想模型中，其他量不变时跨距加倍使位移增至八倍；圆直径加倍使位移降至十六分之一。应解释真实树枝何时不满足这些预测。审查改变控制条件、独立抽样不足、伪重复和无依据推断。<\/p><h3>评估<\/h3><p>个人报告1500字，不含参考文献、表格和附录，建议占单元90%。报告内标准：问题与物理推理15%；设计与可重复性20%；数据分析25%；不确定度与批判评价25%；沟通与诚信15%。提交原始数据、可检查公式或代码、共享数据来源及帮助声明。口头检查建议占10%：解释一个计算、论证一个决策、指出一个改变解释的局限；物理推理、数据解释和批判判断等权。须采用本校评分尺度与规定。<\/p><h3>支持、人工智能与修订<\/h3><p>提供引导电子表格、换算例题和模板，同时提供开放分析路径。拓展关注几何敏感性、不确定度传播或不同模型。因无法实践而使用模拟数据时，实践能力仍需另行取证。 workspace<\/h2><\/header><section id=\"demoControls\"><h2 id=\"nav-section-2\">Automatic classroom demo<\/h2><p><strong>FICTIONAL SAMPLE DATA:<\/strong> Three example students and their answers load automatically when this file opens. The examples include correct answers, unit errors and misconceptions so you can see the dashboard respond. They are not real learner outcomes. Written-response scores remain pending.<\/p><p>The dashboard below is already populated. Open the student activity and use <strong>Submit to tutor<\/strong> to see your response here. This demonstration works inside this file on one device; it is not a multi-device online collection service.<\/p><button id=\"openLab\">Open student lab<\/button><button id=\"closeLab\" hidden>Return to tutor dashboard<\/button><p id=\"linkedStatus\" role=\"status\"><\/p><\/section>\n<section id=\"tools\"><h2 id=\"nav-section-3\">1 · Gather submissions<\/h2><label for=\"files\">Select one or more Sticks_Submission JSON files<\/label><input id=\"files\" type=\"file\" accept=\".json,application/json\" multiple><p class=\"hint\">Students download these files from the interactive lab and send them through your agreed submission route. Files are processed in this browser, without server upload. Import does not prove student identity or prevent editing of submitted data.<\/p><div class=\"teacher-workspace-actions\"><button id=\"backup\">Download teacher backup<\/button><button id=\"csv\">Export gradebook CSV<\/button><button id=\"print\">Print teacher report<\/button><button id=\"save\">Save on this device<\/button><button id=\"clear\">Clear workspace<\/button><\/div><p id=\"status\" aria-live=\"polite\"><\/p><p id=\"errors\" role=\"alert\"><\/p><\/section>\n<section><h2 id=\"nav-section-4\">2 · Class overview<\/h2><div class=\"grid\" id=\"metrics\"><\/div><p class=\"hint\">Scores below are formative practice results: students have access to feedback and answer keys. Written answers are excluded from automatic scores and require rubric review. Class performance alone does not establish teaching effectiveness.<\/p><span class=\"illustration-plan-marker\" id=\"illustration-24\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><\/span><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:760px\"><table><thead><tr><th>Objective question<\/th><th>Correct<\/th><th>Answered<\/th><th>Teaching focus<\/th><\/tr><\/thead><tbody id=\"questionStats\"><\/tbody><\/table><\/div><\/div><div id=\"insights\"><\/div><\/section>\n<section><h2 id=\"nav-section-5\">3 · Student submissions<\/h2><label for=\"search\">Filter by name, ID or group<\/label><input id=\"search\" type=\"search\" placeholder=\"Search students\"><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:950px\"><table><thead><tr><th>Student<\/th><th>Group<\/th><th>Objective score<\/th><th>Written answers<\/th><th>Review<\/th><\/tr><\/thead><tbody id=\"students\"><\/tbody><\/table><\/div><\/div><\/section>\n<section id=\"detail\"><h2 id=\"nav-section-6\">4 · Individual response review<\/h2><p>Select a student to inspect every submitted answer and mark their written work.<\/p><\/section>\n<section><h2 id=\"nav-section-7\">How scoring works<\/h2><p>The dashboard recalculates four objective questions from raw answers rather than trusting the submitted score: stiffness 5,000 N/m, apparent modulus 13.1 GPa and diameter contribution 8%, each with ±2.5% tolerance; the multiple-choice answer must be “fit”. Each is worth one mark. Blank answers score zero and are separately reported.<\/p><p>The written-work rubric covers physical reasoning, design, analysis, evaluation and communication. Teacher marks are reported separately from the 4-mark practice score. This dashboard has no AI model and does not automatically judge written reasoning or laboratory competence. \"<h2>中文教学指南：十五岁学生<\/h2><p><strong>简明翻译版。<\/strong>本版介绍主要课程顺序、概念和评估，并非下方完整英语工作表及评分描述的逐项翻译。<\/p><h3>目标与成果<\/h3><p>探究树枝特征与其表现之间的关系。学生应能描述至少四项特征；使用适当单位测量长度、直径和质量；提出可检验假设；识别变量；实施教师批准的探究；作图；说明两项局限及相应改进。暂以英格兰第四关键阶段科学探究要求为参考，实施时须对照本校实际课程。<\/p><h3>准备与安全<\/h3><p>准备已编号和检查的试样、尺、天平、可用的卡尺、稳定支架及记录表。剔除尖锐、开裂起刺或发霉试样。教师须预先测试跨距和小载荷，使弯曲可测且不造成损坏。不得以折断为目标。手和脸应远离试验区；发现开裂声、滑动或永久变形时立即停止。使用预先收集的材料，避免破坏栖息地。<\/p><h3>第一课：观察与比较，六十分钟<\/h3><p>0–8分钟：描述两根树枝并预测表现。8–16分钟：区分观察与推断，介绍词汇。16–25分钟：示范测量、单位和精度。25–45分钟：检查至少四个试样，轮换测量、记录、器材和核查角色。45–55分钟：比较结果并提出可检验问题。55–60分钟：提交一项观察、一项推断及一项带单位的测量。<\/p><h3>第二课：预测与计划，六十分钟<\/h3><p>核心问题：固定载荷下，直径与弯曲有何关系？将位移定义为中点相对无载位置的垂直移动。确定编号、直径测量位置、跨距、总载荷、加载位置、试样方向、读数时间及重复次数。互评后获得教师批准。树种、含水量、节疤和状态可能混杂比较。重复读取同一试样不等于增加独立试样。<\/p><h3>第三课：探究与分析，六十分钟<\/h3><p>按批准方案记录加载与无载读数并求差。卸载后检查是否恢复，再重复。保持约定条件一致。对有效读数求平均，以直径为横轴、平均位移为纵轴绘制散点图，标注单位并采用均匀刻度。不要按试样顺序连点，也不要仅因结果不符合预测而删除它。若时间不足，应先试行工作量，再减少样本或另设作图时间。<\/p><h3>第四课：评价与应用，六十分钟<\/h3><p>判断证据是否支持假设，引用至少两项结果，说明两项局限及各自改进。为教师指定跨距的小型模型桥构件推荐试样，附示意图，并提出接头、结构布局、重复加载和破坏强度等后续试验。推荐不等于已证明承载能力或桥梁安全。<\/p><h3>核心工作表<\/h3><p>观察记录：试样、长度、直径、质量、纹理、状态和观察。计划：问题、假设、比较变量、测量结果、控制条件、方法、无法控制的因素、停止条件和批准。结果表：试样、直径（毫米）、三次位移（毫米）及平均值；另记跨距、总载荷和读数时间。<\/p><p>平均值＝有效位移读数之和÷有效次数。仅作模拟示例：(4＋5＋3)÷3＝4毫米。不能把模拟数字当作实验结果。在可比条件下弯曲较少，说明该装置下抗弯更强，并不证明断裂载荷更高。<\/p><h3>推理活动<\/h3><p>将陈述分为观察、推断和预测。例如“天平显示24克”是观察；“它可能含水更多”是推断；“相同载荷下它会弯曲更少”是预测。审查一个对粗细树枝使用不同跨距和载荷的错误计划，修正控制条件、读数次数和抽样，并纠正“弯曲最少就总是最结实”的结论。<\/p><h3>评估与答案<\/h3><p>个人成果应包括问题与假设、方法和变量、结果表与图、引用数据的结论、两项局限及改进、以及有依据的建议。可以共享小组数据，但解释必须独立。等效录音展示应保持相同科学要求。<\/p><p>另设十分知识检查：测量结果与单位2分；两个控制条件2分；3、4、5毫米平均值1分；重复与独立试样的区别2分；弯曲与破坏的区别1分；局限及相应改进2分。答案要点：中点垂直位移，毫米等长度单位；跨距和总载荷等控制条件；平均4毫米；重复反映一致性，独立试样反映试样间差异；未测断裂载荷。<\/p><p>探究量规共十五分，五个标准各0–3分：观察与测量、计划、分析、结论与应用、评价。0分表示无相关证据；1分为不完整或不一致；2分为清楚且大体正确；3分为准确、有论证且明确局限，具体以原始描述为准。十五分探究与十分检查分开报告，不能把总分当作经验证的GCSE等级界线。<\/p><h3>支持、人工智能与教学评价<\/h3><p>提供图示词汇、例题、引导表格、建议坐标刻度及适当口头回答方式。拓展可涉及仪器分辨率、变异和控制混杂因素的更强设计。教师可用人工智能起草资料和明确标注的错误示例，但必须核查；学生无需人工智能账户。不要上传可识别个人的作业。实施后查看起始与结束回答、作品、参与、时间和无障碍表现。目前尚未测得学习成效或备课时间节省。<\/p>\", \"<h2>中文教学指南：大学一年级<\/h2><p><strong>简明翻译版。<\/strong>保留核心概念、课程顺序、数值示例和评估标准。下方保留完整英语原版。<\/p><h3>目标与准备<\/h3><p>通过力—位移测量、分析和有限推断，探究树枝作为天然结构材料的表现。假定具备基础代数、国际单位制和作图能力；专门理论在课程中介绍。安排四次两小时课程，另加约六小时自主学习。先检查单位换算、斜率及刚度与破坏强度的区别。试验前，教师必须批准装置、步骤、载荷限制和停止条件。<\/p><h3>模型与局限<\/h3><p>理想中央加载三点弯曲模型：δ＝FL³/(48EI)；k＝dF/dδ；圆截面I＝πd⁴/64；E_app＝kL³/(48I)。区分试样及装置刚度k、材料模量E、抗弯刚度EI和破坏强度。E_app依赖几何、支承、材料和小变形假设；条件不足时仅报告k。锥度、椭圆截面、各向异性、含水量和节疤不能简单当作随机测量噪声。<\/p><h3>第一次课程：表征与理论<\/h3><p>0–15分钟诊断；15–35分钟介绍模型及SI计算；35–70分钟编号并记录质量、长度，以及三个位置各两个垂直方向直径、状态和方向；70–85分钟休息并整理几何；85–105分钟比较试样和假设，区分测量不确定度与生物变异；105–120分钟批判“越粗总是越强”，提交问题和抽样理由。<\/p><h3>第二次课程：方案与试验<\/h3><p>0–15分钟复核假设；15–35分钟审查缺陷方案；35–60分钟设计固定跨距的加载卸载、读数时间和可追溯记录；60–70分钟休息及教师审核；70–100分钟在批准范围内试验，检查分辨率、重复性及恢复；100–120分钟修订方案、分析与排除标准。明确控制条件、独立试样和技术重复。同一试样十个循环不等于十个独立试样。<\/p><h3>第三次课程：测量与分析<\/h3><p>0–10分钟确认设备与限制；10–50分钟采集独立试样数据并适当重复；50–60分钟检查数据完整性；60–85分钟用SI绘制F对δ图，对合理线性范围进行含截距拟合，检查残差及加载卸载差异；85–105分钟估计k及有依据的E_app，分开讨论测量敏感性和试样差异；105–120分钟互评并写有限结论。不得无理由强制零截距，不应隐藏滞回、漂移或残余变形。<\/p><h3>第四次课程：批判与应用<\/h3><p>0–20分钟展示图及局限；20–40分钟核查对照结论的证据与假设；40–65分钟结合刚度、质量和不确定度推荐模型桥构件；65–75分钟休息并准备报告结构；75–100分钟互评；100–115分钟个人口头检查或获批等效形式；115–120分钟提交修改重点和人工智能声明。不能由本试验推断整桥安全或断裂载荷。<\/p><h3>记录与模拟算例<\/h3><p>保留试样和循环编号、添加质量、力、位移、加载或卸载及时间。另记仪器分辨率、零点、附件质量、方向、偏离方案和修正。保留原始数据并说明小组贡献。<\/p><p>单个理想试样的模拟数据：力为0、1、2、3、4牛，位移为0、0.20、0.40、0.60、0.80毫米。L＝0.200米，d＝0.0060米。结果：k＝5牛/毫米＝5000牛/米；I≈6.36×10⁻¹¹米⁴；E_app≈1.31×10¹⁰帕＝13.1吉帕。这些是构造数据，不是实验观察或独立重复。完美直线不能估计真实噪声，也不能验证物理模型。<\/p><h3>不确定度与批判判断<\/h3><p>在圆截面模型、小且相互独立的标准不确定度条件下：u(E)/E≈√[(u(k)/k)²＋(3u(L)/L)²＋(4u(d)/d)²]。直径2%的不确定度单独贡献约8%的模量相对不确定度。此传播式不包含模型偏差、锥度、各向异性或未知含水量。高R²不能验证物理假设，也不能证明破坏强度。<\/p><p>理想模型中，其他量不变时跨距加倍使位移增至八倍；圆直径加倍使位移降至十六分之一。应解释真实树枝何时不满足这些预测。审查改变控制条件、独立抽样不足、伪重复和无依据推断。<\/p><h3>评估<\/h3><p>个人报告1500字，不含参考文献、表格和附录，建议占单元90%。报告内标准：问题与物理推理15%；设计与可重复性20%；数据分析25%；不确定度与批判评价25%；沟通与诚信15%。提交原始数据、可检查公式或代码、共享数据来源及帮助声明。口头检查建议占10%：解释一个计算、论证一个决策、指出一个改变解释的局限；物理推理、数据解释和批判判断等权。须采用本校评分尺度与规定。<\/p><h3>支持、人工智能与修订<\/h3><p>提供引导电子表格、换算例题和模板，同时提供开放分析路径。拓展关注几何敏感性、不确定度传播或不同模型。因无法实践而使用模拟数据时，实践能力仍需另行取证。 Repetir lecturas no equivale a añadir muestras independientes.<\/p><h3>Clase 3 · Investigar y analizar · 60 minutos<\/h3><p>Siga el procedimiento aprobado, registre lecturas con y sin carga y calcule su diferencia. Compruebe la recuperación al retirar la carga antes de repetir. Mantenga constantes las condiciones acordadas. Calcule la media de las lecturas válidas y represente diámetro en el eje horizontal y desplazamiento medio en el vertical, con unidades y escalas regulares. No una los puntos por orden de muestra ni elimine un resultado solo porque contradice la predicción. Si el tiempo no basta, reduzca el número de muestras o separe la sesión de gráficos tras probar la carga de trabajo.<\/p><h3>Clase 4 · Evaluar y aplicar · 60 minutos<\/h3><p>Determine si las pruebas apoyan la hipótesis. Cite al menos dos resultados, explique dos limitaciones y una mejora relacionada para cada una. Recomiende muestras para miembros de un pequeño puente de maqueta con una luz indicada por el docente. Incluya un boceto y nuevas pruebas necesarias: uniones, configuración, cargas repetidas y resistencia a la rotura. La recomendación no demuestra capacidad de carga ni seguridad del puente.<\/p><h3>Hojas de trabajo esenciales<\/h3><p>Registro: muestra; longitud; diámetro; masa; textura; estado; observaciones. Plan: pregunta; hipótesis; variable comparada; resultado medido; controles; método; factores no controlados; condiciones de parada; aprobación. Resultados: muestra; diámetro en mm; desplazamientos 1, 2 y 3 en mm; media. Registre también luz, carga total y tiempo de lectura.<\/p><p>Media = suma de desplazamientos válidos ÷ número de lecturas válidas. Ejemplo simulado: (4 + 5 + 3) ÷ 3 = 4 mm. No copie datos simulados como resultados experimentales. Una menor flexión en condiciones equivalentes indica mayor resistencia a la flexión en ese montaje, no mayor carga de rotura.<\/p><h3>Actividades de razonamiento<\/h3><p>Clasifique observaciones, inferencias y predicciones. Ejemplos: «la balanza indica 24 g» es una observación; «puede contener más humedad» es una inferencia; «con la misma carga se doblará menos» es una predicción. Audite un plan que usa distinta carga y separación entre apoyos para palos gruesos y finos. Corrija controles, lecturas, muestreo y la conclusión errónea de que el que menos se dobla es siempre el más resistente.<\/p><h3>Evaluación y respuestas<\/h3><p>Producto final individual: pregunta e hipótesis, método y variables, tabla y gráfico, conclusión con resultados, dos limitaciones y mejoras, y recomendación justificada. Puede utilizar datos de grupo, pero la explicación debe ser individual; una presentación grabada equivalente conserva las mismas exigencias.<\/p><p>Prueba separada de 10 puntos: resultado medido y unidad, 2; dos controles, 2; media de 3, 4 y 5 mm, 1; diferencia entre repetición y muestras independientes, 2; diferencia entre flexión y rotura, 1; limitación y mejora relacionada, 2. Respuestas: desplazamiento vertical del punto medio en mm; controles como luz y carga; media de 4 mm; las repeticiones informan de consistencia, las muestras independientes de variación entre muestras; no se midió la carga de rotura.<\/p><p>Rúbrica de investigación: cinco criterios, de 0 a 3 puntos cada uno, total 15: observación y medición; planificación; análisis; conclusión y aplicación; evaluación. 0: sin evidencia pertinente. 1: evidencia parcial o inconsistente. 2: evidencia clara y mayoritariamente correcta. 3: evidencia precisa, justificada y con límites explícitos, según los descriptores originales. Informe los 15 puntos y la prueba de 10 por separado; no son límites de calificación GCSE validados.<\/p><h3>Apoyo, IA y evaluación de la enseñanza<\/h3><p>Use vocabulario visual, ejemplos, tablas guiadas, escalas sugeridas y respuestas orales cuando proceda. Amplíe mediante resolución instrumental, variación y diseños que controlen factores de confusión. La IA manejada por el docente puede ayudar a redactar recursos y ejemplos deliberadamente erróneos, siempre revisados y etiquetados; no se requieren cuentas del alumnado. Compruebe afirmaciones científicas y no suba trabajos identificables. Tras impartir, revise respuestas iniciales y finales, trabajos, participación, tiempos y accesibilidad. No se han medido aún resultados de aprendizaje ni ahorro de tiempo.<\/p>\", \"university\": \"<h2>Guía docente en español: primer curso universitario<\/h2><p><strong>Edición concisa traducida.<\/strong> Conserva los conceptos, la secuencia, el ejemplo numérico y los criterios centrales. Se presuponen álgebra básica, unidades SI y gráficos; la teoría especializada se introduce en la unidad. Cuatro sesiones de dos horas más unas seis horas autónomas. La estimación E_app depende de supuestos sobre geometría, apoyos, material y pequeña deformación; informe solo k cuando no sea defendible. Conicidad, ovalidad, anisotropía, humedad y nudos no son simplemente ruido aleatorio de medición.<\/p><h3>Sesión 1 · Caracterización y teoría<\/h3><p>0–15: diagnóstico. 15–35: modelo y cálculo SI. 35–70: identificar muestras y registrar masa, longitud y dos diámetros perpendiculares en tres posiciones, con orientación y estado. 70–85: descanso y resumen geométrico. 85–105: comparar y formular hipótesis, distinguiendo incertidumbre de medición y variación biológica. 105–120: criticar «más grueso siempre significa más fuerte» y entregar pregunta y justificación del muestreo.<\/p><h3>Sesión 2 · Protocolo y prueba piloto<\/h3><p>0–15: revisar hipótesis. 15–35: auditar un protocolo defectuoso. 35–60: diseñar ciclos de carga y descarga con luz fija, tiempos y registro trazable. 60–70: revisión y descanso. 70–100: prueba piloto con límites aprobados, comprobando resolución, repetibilidad y recuperación. 100–120: revisar protocolo, análisis y criterios de exclusión. No deduzca seguridad estructural ni carga de rotura a partir de este ensayo.<\/p><h3>Registro y ejemplo simulado<\/h3><p>Conserve identificación de muestra y ciclo, masa añadida, fuerza, desplazamiento, carga/descarga y tiempo. \"<h2>中文教学指南：十五岁学生<\/h2><p><strong>简明翻译版。<\/strong>本版介绍主要课程顺序、概念和评估，并非下方完整英语工作表及评分描述的逐项翻译。<\/p><h3>目标与成果<\/h3><p>探究树枝特征与其表现之间的关系。学生应能描述至少四项特征；使用适当单位测量长度、直径和质量；提出可检验假设；识别变量；实施教师批准的探究；作图；说明两项局限及相应改进。暂以英格兰第四关键阶段科学探究要求为参考，实施时须对照本校实际课程。<\/p><h3>准备与安全<\/h3><p>准备已编号和检查的试样、尺、天平、可用的卡尺、稳定支架及记录表。剔除尖锐、开裂起刺或发霉试样。教师须预先测试跨距和小载荷，使弯曲可测且不造成损坏。不得以折断为目标。手和脸应远离试验区；发现开裂声、滑动或永久变形时立即停止。使用预先收集的材料，避免破坏栖息地。<\/p><h3>第一课：观察与比较，六十分钟<\/h3><p>0–8分钟：描述两根树枝并预测表现。8–16分钟：区分观察与推断，介绍词汇。16–25分钟：示范测量、单位和精度。25–45分钟：检查至少四个试样，轮换测量、记录、器材和核查角色。45–55分钟：比较结果并提出可检验问题。55–60分钟：提交一项观察、一项推断及一项带单位的测量。<\/p><h3>第二课：预测与计划，六十分钟<\/h3><p>核心问题：固定载荷下，直径与弯曲有何关系？将位移定义为中点相对无载位置的垂直移动。确定编号、直径测量位置、跨距、总载荷、加载位置、试样方向、读数时间及重复次数。互评后获得教师批准。树种、含水量、节疤和状态可能混杂比较。重复读取同一试样不等于增加独立试样。<\/p><h3>第三课：探究与分析，六十分钟<\/h3><p>按批准方案记录加载与无载读数并求差。卸载后检查是否恢复，再重复。保持约定条件一致。对有效读数求平均，以直径为横轴、平均位移为纵轴绘制散点图，标注单位并采用均匀刻度。不要按试样顺序连点，也不要仅因结果不符合预测而删除它。若时间不足，应先试行工作量，再减少样本或另设作图时间。<\/p><h3>第四课：评价与应用，六十分钟<\/h3><p>判断证据是否支持假设，引用至少两项结果，说明两项局限及各自改进。为教师指定跨距的小型模型桥构件推荐试样，附示意图，并提出接头、结构布局、重复加载和破坏强度等后续试验。推荐不等于已证明承载能力或桥梁安全。<\/p><h3>核心工作表<\/h3><p>观察记录：试样、长度、直径、质量、纹理、状态和观察。计划：问题、假设、比较变量、测量结果、控制条件、方法、无法控制的因素、停止条件和批准。结果表：试样、直径（毫米）、三次位移（毫米）及平均值；另记跨距、总载荷和读数时间。<\/p><p>平均值＝有效位移读数之和÷有效次数。仅作模拟示例：(4＋5＋3)÷3＝4毫米。不能把模拟数字当作实验结果。在可比条件下弯曲较少，说明该装置下抗弯更强，并不证明断裂载荷更高。<\/p><h3>推理活动<\/h3><p>将陈述分为观察、推断和预测。例如“天平显示24克”是观察；“它可能含水更多”是推断；“相同载荷下它会弯曲更少”是预测。审查一个对粗细树枝使用不同跨距和载荷的错误计划，修正控制条件、读数次数和抽样，并纠正“弯曲最少就总是最结实”的结论。<\/p><h3>评估与答案<\/h3><p>个人成果应包括问题与假设、方法和变量、结果表与图、引用数据的结论、两项局限及改进、以及有依据的建议。可以共享小组数据，但解释必须独立。等效录音展示应保持相同科学要求。<\/p><p>另设十分知识检查：测量结果与单位2分；两个控制条件2分；3、4、5毫米平均值1分；重复与独立试样的区别2分；弯曲与破坏的区别1分；局限及相应改进2分。答案要点：中点垂直位移，毫米等长度单位；跨距和总载荷等控制条件；平均4毫米；重复反映一致性，独立试样反映试样间差异；未测断裂载荷。<\/p><p>探究量规共十五分，五个标准各0–3分：观察与测量、计划、分析、结论与应用、评价。0分表示无相关证据；1分为不完整或不一致；2分为清楚且大体正确；3分为准确、有论证且明确局限，具体以原始描述为准。十五分探究与十分检查分开报告，不能把总分当作经验证的GCSE等级界线。<\/p><h3>支持、人工智能与教学评价<\/h3><p>提供图示词汇、例题、引导表格、建议坐标刻度及适当口头回答方式。拓展可涉及仪器分辨率、变异和控制混杂因素的更强设计。教师可用人工智能起草资料和明确标注的错误示例，但必须核查；学生无需人工智能账户。不要上传可识别个人的作业。实施后查看起始与结束回答、作品、参与、时间和无障碍表现。目前尚未测得学习成效或备课时间节省。<\/p>\", \"<h2>中文教学指南：大学一年级<\/h2><p><strong>简明翻译版。<\/strong>保留核心概念、课程顺序、数值示例和评估标准。下方保留完整英语原版。<\/p><h3>目标与准备<\/h3><p>通过力—位移测量、分析和有限推断，探究树枝作为天然结构材料的表现。假定具备基础代数、国际单位制和作图能力；专门理论在课程中介绍。安排四次两小时课程，另加约六小时自主学习。先检查单位换算、斜率及刚度与破坏强度的区别。试验前，教师必须批准装置、步骤、载荷限制和停止条件。<\/p><h3>模型与局限<\/h3><p>理想中央加载三点弯曲模型：δ＝FL³/(48EI)；k＝dF/dδ；圆截面I＝πd⁴/64；E_app＝kL³/(48I)。区分试样及装置刚度k、材料模量E、抗弯刚度EI和破坏强度。E_app依赖几何、支承、材料和小变形假设；条件不足时仅报告k。锥度、椭圆截面、各向异性、含水量和节疤不能简单当作随机测量噪声。<\/p><h3>第一次课程：表征与理论<\/h3><p>0–15分钟诊断；15–35分钟介绍模型及SI计算；35–70分钟编号并记录质量、长度，以及三个位置各两个垂直方向直径、状态和方向；70–85分钟休息并整理几何；85–105分钟比较试样和假设，区分测量不确定度与生物变异；105–120分钟批判“越粗总是越强”，提交问题和抽样理由。<\/p><h3>第二次课程：方案与试验<\/h3><p>0–15分钟复核假设；15–35分钟审查缺陷方案；35–60分钟设计固定跨距的加载卸载、读数时间和可追溯记录；60–70分钟休息及教师审核；70–100分钟在批准范围内试验，检查分辨率、重复性及恢复；100–120分钟修订方案、分析与排除标准。明确控制条件、独立试样和技术重复。同一试样十个循环不等于十个独立试样。<\/p><h3>第三次课程：测量与分析<\/h3><p>0–10分钟确认设备与限制；10–50分钟采集独立试样数据并适当重复；50–60分钟检查数据完整性；60–85分钟用SI绘制F对δ图，对合理线性范围进行含截距拟合，检查残差及加载卸载差异；85–105分钟估计k及有依据的E_app，分开讨论测量敏感性和试样差异；105–120分钟互评并写有限结论。不得无理由强制零截距，不应隐藏滞回、漂移或残余变形。<\/p><h3>第四次课程：批判与应用<\/h3><p>0–20分钟展示图及局限；20–40分钟核查对照结论的证据与假设；40–65分钟结合刚度、质量和不确定度推荐模型桥构件；65–75分钟休息并准备报告结构；75–100分钟互评；100–115分钟个人口头检查或获批等效形式；115–120分钟提交修改重点和人工智能声明。不能由本试验推断整桥安全或断裂载荷。<\/p><h3>记录与模拟算例<\/h3><p>保留试样和循环编号、添加质量、力、位移、加载或卸载及时间。另记仪器分辨率、零点、附件质量、方向、偏离方案和修正。保留原始数据并说明小组贡献。<\/p><p>单个理想试样的模拟数据：力为0、1、2、3、4牛，位移为0、0.20、0.40、0.60、0.80毫米。L＝0.200米，d＝0.0060米。结果：k＝5牛/毫米＝5000牛/米；I≈6.36×10⁻¹¹米⁴；E_app≈1.31×10¹⁰帕＝13.1吉帕。这些是构造数据，不是实验观察或独立重复。完美直线不能估计真实噪声，也不能验证物理模型。<\/p><h3>不确定度与批判判断<\/h3><p>在圆截面模型、小且相互独立的标准不确定度条件下：u(E)/E≈√[(u(k)/k)²＋(3u(L)/L)²＋(4u(d)/d)²]。直径2%的不确定度单独贡献约8%的模量相对不确定度。此传播式不包含模型偏差、锥度、各向异性或未知含水量。高R²不能验证物理假设，也不能证明破坏强度。<\/p><p>理想模型中，其他量不变时跨距加倍使位移增至八倍；圆直径加倍使位移降至十六分之一。应解释真实树枝何时不满足这些预测。审查改变控制条件、独立抽样不足、伪重复和无依据推断。<\/p><h3>评估<\/h3><p>个人报告1500字，不含参考文献、表格和附录，建议占单元90%。报告内标准：问题与物理推理15%；设计与可重复性20%；数据分析25%；不确定度与批判评价25%；沟通与诚信15%。提交原始数据、可检查公式或代码、共享数据来源及帮助声明。口头检查建议占10%：解释一个计算、论证一个决策、指出一个改变解释的局限；物理推理、数据解释和批判判断等权。须采用本校评分尺度与规定。<\/p><h3>支持、人工智能与修订<\/h3><p>提供引导电子表格、换算例题和模板，同时提供开放分析路径。拓展关注几何敏感性、不确定度传播或不同模型。因无法实践而使用模拟数据时，实践能力仍需另行取证。 style=\"grid-column:1/-1\" hidden><\/section><main class=\"shell\" id=\"mainContent\"><p><a href=\"learning-materials.html#nav-section-1\">← Back to teaching materials<\/a><\/p><div class=\"anchorLinks\"><\/div><article class=\"card\"><div class=\"reader\"><h3 id=\"heading-0\">Investigating sticks as natural structural materials<\/h3><p>First year undergraduate teaching and learning pack<\/p><p>An introductory laboratory unit in natural materials, experimental design and evidence-based modelling. Four two-hour sessions combine specimen characterisation, non-destructive bending, quantitative analysis and critical evaluation of AI-generated claims. Allow approximately six additional hours for reading, analysis and the individual report.<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-1\">Contents<\/h3><p class=\"project-index-row\"><a class=\"project-index-link\" href=\"#heading-4\">1 Planning and preparation<\/a><\/p><p class=\"project-index-row\"><a class=\"project-index-link\" href=\"#heading-10\">2 Unit outline and assessment strategy<\/a><\/p><p class=\"project-index-row\"><a class=\"project-index-link\" href=\"#heading-14\">3 Detailed teaching plans<\/a><\/p><p class=\"project-index-row\"><a class=\"project-index-link\" href=\"#heading-22\">4 Student handouts worksheets and visual aids<\/a><\/p><p class=\"project-index-row\"><a class=\"project-index-link\" href=\"#heading-34\">5 Assessment brief rubric and teacher guidance<\/a><\/p><p class=\"project-index-row\"><a class=\"project-index-link\" href=\"#heading-42\">6 Teaching evaluation and future application<\/a><\/p><h3 id=\"heading-2\">Using this pack<\/h3><p>Designed for a first-year engineering, materials science or interdisciplinary science module. Students should have basic algebra, SI units and graphing skills. Beam theory is introduced within the unit; prior specialist mechanics is not assumed. Local programme outcomes and assessment regulations take precedence over the suggested mapping and weights.<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-3\">AI integration key<\/h3><p>[AI PREPARATION] Tutor drafts or adapts resources using AI and verifies them.<\/p><p>[AI CLASSROOM] Students critique labelled AI-generated examples.<\/p><p>[AI OPTIONAL] Institution-approved student use with disclosure and independent verification; an equivalent non-AI route is available.<\/p><p>[AI REVIEW] Tutor uses anonymised patterns of difficulty to draft follow-up work.<\/p><p>No AI subscription or student account is required. Raw measurements must be collected honestly, and simulated data must remain clearly labelled. Classroom outcomes have not yet been measured.<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-4\">1 Planning and preparation<\/h3><h4 id=\"heading-5\">Topic rationale and audience<\/h4><p>Fallen sticks provide a low-cost context in which an apparently simple mechanical question becomes an authentic problem of geometry, biological variability and model validity. Students distinguish specimen stiffness from material modulus and failure strength, then examine whether an ideal beam model can usefully describe irregular natural samples.<\/p><p>The cohort may include different mathematical preparation, laboratory experience, language backgrounds and access needs. A short diagnostic task establishes support needs. Provide an algebra refresher, accessible digital worksheets, flexible laboratory roles and alternatives to manual handling. Maintain common intellectual expectations while varying scaffolding.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-6\">Learning outcomes and programme mapping<\/h4><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:570px\"><table><tr><th>By the end students will be able to<\/th><th>Suggested first year outcome area<\/th><th>Evidence<\/th><\/tr><tr><td>Characterise geometry and condition with traceable measurements and stated resolution.<\/td><td>Laboratory measurement and quantitative literacy<\/td><td>Specimen log and raw data<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Design a controlled investigation distinguishing technical repeats from independent specimens.<\/td><td>Experimental design and scientific reasoning<\/td><td>Approved protocol<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Estimate specimen bending stiffness from force–deflection data and evaluate linearity.<\/td><td>Introductory mechanics and data analysis<\/td><td>Graphs, fit and residuals<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Estimate apparent modulus only when geometry and model assumptions are defensible.<\/td><td>Mathematical modelling and limitations<\/td><td>Worked calculations and qualification<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Evaluate uncertainty, confounding and the scope of evidence.<\/td><td>Critical analysis<\/td><td>Individual report<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Audit an AI-generated scientific claim and disclose any AI assistance.<\/td><td>Digital and research literacy<\/td><td>Verification appendix<\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><\/div><p>This is a proposed alignment to generic first-year outcomes, not accreditation or a claim of compliance with a named university standard. Replace the mapping with the module’s approved outcomes before formal adoption.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-7\">Tools and rationale<\/h4><p>Use ChatGPT or another institution-approved text model for draft explanations, contrasting methods and critique prompts. No model comparison has been conducted. Use a spreadsheet or a transparent Python notebook for calculations, regression and plotting, retaining formulas or code for inspection. Calculations must be checked against worked examples. AI-generated prose is not a scientific reference.<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-8\">Laboratory preparation and scientific model<\/h3><p>The tutor pilots the apparatus, determines safe load increments and a measurable displacement range, and approves the protocol. Use stable rounded supports, a centred loading attachment, a displacement gauge or suitable measuring system, callipers, a balance and inspected specimens. Record loading hardware mass. Do not prescribe universal loads for variable natural samples.<\/p><span class=\"illustration-plan-marker\" id=\"illustration-32\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><\/span><p>Use non-destructive loading only; stop for cracking, slipping, residual deformation or departure from the approved range.<\/p><p>Keep loads close to the bench, retain falling loads where appropriate and keep hands and faces clear. Follow local laboratory risk assessment and eye-protection requirements.<\/p><p>Select reasonably straight specimens and document species if verified, visible defects, bark, curvature and conditioning. Unknown species or moisture must be recorded as unknown.<\/p><p>Where feasible use at least three independent specimens per comparison group. If availability prevents this, limit claims to tested specimens rather than making population inferences.<\/p><p>Agree a fixed span, orientation and reading time. Record several cross-sections and orthogonal diameters; do not hide taper or ovality inside one unqualified diameter.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-9\">Model handout<\/h4><p>For a simply supported, slender, prismatic beam with a central point force, small deflection and linear elastic behaviour:<\/p><p>δ = F L³ / (48 E I)     k = dF/dδ     E_app = k L³ / (48 I)<\/p><p>For a solid circular section: I = π d⁴ / 64. Here δ is midpoint displacement (m), F is applied force (N), L is support span (m), E is modulus (Pa), I is second moment of area (m⁴), and k is specimen stiffness (N/m). Use F = mg, with g = 9.81 m/s² and total added mass in kg.<\/p><p>These equations are an idealisation. Natural sticks may be tapered, curved, anisotropic, heterogeneous or damaged. Support indentation, slip, shear effects, loading history and creep can affect readings. E_app is an apparent estimate under the adopted model, not automatically a species-level material constant. If geometry is not adequately represented, report k and model limitations instead of forcing a modulus estimate.<\/p><p>Source: University of Cambridge, The Three Point Bend Test, theory note. https://mi.eng.cam.ac.uk/IALego/bender_files/bend_theory.pdf<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-10\">2 Unit outline and assessment strategy<\/h3><h4 id=\"heading-11\">Topic introduction<\/h4><p>Two similar-looking sticks can behave differently under load. Is the difference caused by geometry, material structure, moisture or the measurement method? This unit uses that question to explore the relationship between experimental evidence and an ideal mechanical model. A useful investigation may reveal where the model fails as well as where it works.<\/p><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:570px\"><table><tr><th>Session<\/th><th>Progression<\/th><th>Preparation and evidence<\/th><\/tr><tr><td><a class=\"project-index-link\" href=\"#heading-14\">1 Characterisation and theory<\/a><\/td><td>Move from description to quantified geometry, uncertainty and a testable question.<\/td><td>Read model handout; produce specimen log and draft hypothesis.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td><a class=\"project-index-link\" href=\"#heading-16\">2 Protocol and pilot<\/a><\/td><td>Translate the question into a repeatable, approved method.<\/td><td>Protocol, sampling rationale and pilot record.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td><a class=\"project-index-link\" href=\"#heading-18\">3 Measurement and analysis<\/a><\/td><td>Collect force–deflection series; estimate stiffness and assess fit.<\/td><td>Raw dataset, graphs, residuals and qualified estimates.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td><a class=\"project-index-link\" href=\"#heading-20\">4 Critique and application<\/a><\/td><td>Defend conclusions, audit AI claims and make a bounded design recommendation.<\/td><td>Peer review, oral explanation and individual report plan.<\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><\/div><h4 id=\"heading-12\">Assessment approach<\/h4><p>Diagnostic: SI conversions, graph gradients and a stiffness-versus-strength question before Session 1. Formative: specimen-log feedback, method approval, analysis checkpoints and peer critique. Summative: an individual 1,500-word laboratory report with raw-data and calculation appendices, plus a brief individual oral check. Suggested weighting is 90% report and 10% oral check, subject to module regulations.<\/p><p>Reports must include a question, theory and assumptions, sampling and method, raw-data provenance, uncertainty, analysis, discussion, a limited design recommendation and an AI-use statement. Shared group measurements are permitted when collaborators and contributions are identified. Analysis and interpretation must demonstrate individual understanding.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-13\">Differentiation and access<\/h4><p>Offer a scaffolded spreadsheet alongside an open analysis route. Provide unit-conversion examples and a protocol template, then gradually remove prompts. Extend confident students through geometry sensitivity, uncertainty propagation or competing fits rather than additional routine work. Recorded explanations, accessible apparatus and alternative data-handling roles should preserve equivalent outcomes. Use the labelled simulated dataset only when practical access is unavailable and acknowledge that practical competence then needs separate evidence.<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-14\">3 Session 1 Characterisation and introductory theory<\/h3><h4 id=\"heading-15\">Learning objectives<\/h4><p>Record specimen geometry and instrument resolution.<\/p><p>Explain the distinction between k, E and strength.<\/p><p>State a testable question with relevant confounders.<\/p><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:720px\"><table class=\"readable-timing\"><tr><th>Minutes<\/th><th>Activity<\/th><th>Assessment<\/th><\/tr><tr><td>0–15<\/td><td>Diagnostic quiz and discussion of entry knowledge.<\/td><td>Check units, gradients and property distinctions.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>15–35<\/td><td>Introduce beam model and assumptions. Work through one SI calculation.<\/td><td>Students annotate each variable and check dimensions.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>35–70<\/td><td>Groups label specimens; measure mass, length and two diameters at three positions. Record visible condition and orientation.<\/td><td>Tutor checks traceability, instrument reading and treatment of irregularity.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>70–85<\/td><td>Break and preparation of geometry summaries.<\/td><td>Check completeness of logs.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>85–105<\/td><td>Compare specimens and draft hypotheses. Discuss measurement uncertainty versus biological variation.<\/td><td>Each student identifies a confounder and its consequence.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>105–120<\/td><td>[AI CLASSROOM] Critique the claim that thicker always means stronger. Submit a question and sampling rationale.<\/td><td>Written explanation distinguishes geometry, stiffness and failure.<\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><\/div><p>[AI PREPARATION] Draft vocabulary and contrasting explanations, then check equations and terminology. Support: SI conversion sheet and annotated formula. Extension: evaluate why diameter error is amplified in I.<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-16\">3 Session 2 Protocol design and pilot<\/h3><h4 id=\"heading-17\">Learning objectives<\/h4><p>Specify controls, sampling and technical repeats.<\/p><p>Pilot a safe force–deflection procedure.<\/p><p>Set explicit criteria for retaining or qualifying results.<\/p><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:720px\"><table class=\"readable-timing\"><tr><th>Minutes<\/th><th>Activity<\/th><th>Assessment<\/th><\/tr><tr><td>0–15<\/td><td>Review hypotheses and confounders.<\/td><td>Check the question is answerable with available specimens.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>15–35<\/td><td>[AI CLASSROOM] Audit the flawed protocol in the resource section.<\/td><td>Identify pseudoreplication, changed controls and unsupported inference.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>35–60<\/td><td>Design fixed-span loading and unloading series, reading times and raw-data structure.<\/td><td>Tutor checks calibration or zero checks and total applied force.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>60–70<\/td><td>Break; tutor reviews proposed procedure.<\/td><td>Method must be approved before pilot testing.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>70–100<\/td><td>Pilot within tutor-defined limits. Check displacement resolution, repeatability and return after unloading.<\/td><td>Record pilot changes and reasons.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>100–120<\/td><td>Revise protocol and pre-specify analysis and exclusion criteria.<\/td><td>Submit approved protocol with independent-sample count.<\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><\/div><p>[AI OPTIONAL] Ask an approved model to identify missing controls in a de-identified protocol, then accept or reject each suggestion with reasons. Non-AI route: use the same tutor checklist. Support: protocol headings. Extension: plan a span-sensitivity check.<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-18\">3 Session 3 Experimental measurement and quantitative analysis<\/h3><h4 id=\"heading-19\">Learning objectives<\/h4><p>Collect traceable loading and unloading data.<\/p><p>Estimate k and examine residuals.<\/p><p>Report uncertainty and qualify any E_app estimate.<\/p><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:720px\"><table class=\"readable-timing\"><tr><th>Minutes<\/th><th>Activity<\/th><th>Assessment<\/th><\/tr><tr><td>0–10<\/td><td>Confirm apparatus checks and stop conditions.<\/td><td>Students explain safe operating limits.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>10–50<\/td><td>Collect approved force steps for independent specimens, with repeat cycles where feasible. Log time, displacement, orientation and anomalies.<\/td><td>Tutor observes individual technique and verifies early records.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>50–60<\/td><td>Break and data-integrity check.<\/td><td>Preserve raw data; document all corrections.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>60–85<\/td><td>Plot F against δ in SI units. Fit a justified linear range with an intercept; inspect residuals and loading/unloading differences.<\/td><td>Check axes, slope units, fit range and signs of nonlinearity.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>85–105<\/td><td>Estimate stiffness and, where justified, E_app. Quantify measurement sensitivity and sample variation separately.<\/td><td>Independent calculation check; qualify geometry assumptions.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>105–120<\/td><td>Pairs challenge each other’s analysis and write a bounded conclusion.<\/td><td>Exit response identifies one supported claim and one unresolved limitation.<\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><\/div><p>[AI OPTIONAL] AI may explain an error message or suggest a plot, but students inspect all code and verify outputs. No invented or silently replaced data. Support: spreadsheet formulas and worked fit. Extension: propagate uncertainty and compare models.<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-20\">3 Session 4 Scientific critique and design application<\/h3><h4 id=\"heading-21\">Learning objectives<\/h4><p>Defend a conclusion using quantitative evidence.<\/p><p>Evaluate model validity and an AI-generated claim.<\/p><p>Recommend material selection within the limits of the test.<\/p><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:720px\"><table class=\"readable-timing\"><tr><th>Minutes<\/th><th>Activity<\/th><th>Assessment<\/th><\/tr><tr><td>0–20<\/td><td>Groups present one graph and one major limitation.<\/td><td>Tutor probes individual understanding.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>20–40<\/td><td>[AI CLASSROOM] Compare the labelled conclusions and verify the unsupported statements.<\/td><td>Record claim, evidence, correction and verification source.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>40–65<\/td><td>Develop a model-bridge member recommendation using stiffness, mass, uncertainty and further-test requirements.<\/td><td>Check that breaking load and assembled safety are not inferred.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>65–75<\/td><td>Break and preparation of report outline.<\/td><td>Check report components.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>75–100<\/td><td>Structured peer review of methods, graph and discussion.<\/td><td>Feedback must identify a specific issue and improvement.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>100–115<\/td><td>Individual oral checks or short recorded explanations.<\/td><td>Assess physical reasoning, data interpretation and limitations.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>115–120<\/td><td>Submit revision priorities and AI-use statement.<\/td><td>Check disclosure and an actionable next step.<\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><\/div><p>[AI REVIEW] Use anonymised misconceptions to draft follow-up exercises. Support: report structure and evidence prompts. Extension: design an independent experiment separating geometry from material variability.<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-22\">4 Student handout and specimen worksheet<\/h3><p>Name __________________ Group __________ Date __________<\/p><p>Define these in your own words: specimen stiffness k; material modulus E; flexural rigidity EI; strength; independent specimen; technical repeat; confounder. Consult the model handout, then explain why they are not interchangeable.<\/p><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:950px\"><table><tr><th>Specimen ID<\/th><th>Length mm<\/th><th>Mass g<\/th><th>Diameters at 3 positions mm<\/th><th>Condition and orientation<\/th><\/tr><tr><td>A<\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td>B<\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td>C<\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td>D<\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><\/div><p>At each position record two perpendicular diameters and label their orientation. Record instrument resolution and any zero offset separately. Explain whether a circular approximation is defensible; do not treat ovality or taper as random measurement noise.<\/p><p>Hypothesis and rationale:<\/p><p>Sampling strategy, independent specimen count and limits on generalisation:<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-23\">Protocol and results worksheets<\/h3><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:480px\"><table><tr><th>Protocol decision<\/th><th>Record your choice and justification<\/th><\/tr><tr><td>Question and comparison variables<\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Span, support type and sample orientation<\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Force steps and total hardware mass<\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Displacement system and zero check<\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Reading time and loading/unloading order<\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Technical repeats and independent specimens<\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Stop conditions and exclusion rules<\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><\/div><p>Tutor approval __________________ Date __________<\/p><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:950px\"><table><tr><th>Specimen and cycle<\/th><th>Added mass kg<\/th><th>Force N<\/th><th>Displacement mm<\/th><th>Load or unload and time<\/th><\/tr><tr><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><\/div><p>Duplicate this table as required. Keep the original raw data, note corrections transparently and log deviations from the approved method. Use unloaded baselines consistently and account for any preload in the force definition.<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-24\">Analysis worksheet and simulated practice data<\/h3><p>SIMULATED PRACTICE DATA ONLY. These values describe one idealised specimen; they are not experimental observations or independent replicates.<\/p><span class=\"illustration-plan-marker\" id=\"illustration-34\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><\/span><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:480px\"><table><tr><th>Force N<\/th><th>Midpoint displacement mm<\/th><\/tr><tr><td>0<\/td><td>0.00<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>1<\/td><td>0.20<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>2<\/td><td>0.40<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>3<\/td><td>0.60<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>4<\/td><td>0.80<\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><\/div><p>For this practice example use L = 0.200 m and circular diameter d = 0.0060 m. Convert displacement to metres, plot F against δ, determine k, calculate I and estimate E_app. Explain why a perfect line gives no estimate of real experimental scatter.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-25\">Apply to your measured data<\/h4><p>Plot individual specimens separately or clearly label them. Do not pool repeated points as independent specimens.<\/p><p>Fit a justified linear range; report slope and units, intercept, fit range and residuals. Do not force zero intercept without physical and measurement justification.<\/p><p>Compare loading and unloading. Describe drift, hysteresis or residual displacement rather than hiding it.<\/p><p>Record how geometry was approximated. Report k alone when E_app would imply unjustified precision.<\/p><p>Separate instrument uncertainty, repeatability and specimen-to-specimen variability. A large R² does not validate the physical model.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-26\">Uncertainty extension<\/h4><p>For independent small standard uncertainties under the circular model, u(E)/E ≈ √[(u(k)/k)² + (3u(L)/L)² + (4u(d)/d)²]. State the assumptions. This propagation does not capture model bias, taper, anisotropy or unknown moisture. A 2% diameter uncertainty contributes approximately 8% relative uncertainty to E on its own.<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-27\">Visual aids and interactive activities<\/h3><img alt=\"Three-point bending setup with two supports, a central load and midpoint displacement\" style=\"width:100%;max-width:800px;height:auto\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><p>Conceptual three-point bending setup, not to scale. The solid line indicates the unloaded specimen and the dashed line a displaced shape. Tutor-approved apparatus and loading limits govern practical work.<\/p><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:570px\"><table><tr><th>Quantity<\/th><th>Depends on<\/th><th>Interpretation<\/th><\/tr><tr><td>k = dF/dδ<\/td><td>Material, geometry, span and boundary conditions<\/td><td>Specimen and setup response<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>E_app = kL³/(48I)<\/td><td>Measured k plus idealised beam and geometry assumptions<\/td><td>Qualified material-model estimate<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Failure strength<\/td><td>Failure criterion and destructive test conditions<\/td><td>Not established by this experiment<\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><\/div><h4 id=\"heading-28\">Activity 1 Protocol audit in pairs<\/h4><p>[AI CLASSROOM — DELIBERATELY FLAWED] “Test one thick stick on a short span and one thin stick on a long span. Measure each ten times. Treat the twenty readings as twenty independent specimens. The highest stiffness proves the highest breaking strength.” Identify at least five problems and propose a corrected design.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-29\">Activity 2 Model challenge<\/h4><p>Predict the effect of doubling span or doubling circular diameter while holding other model quantities fixed. Explain why the prediction may fail for real sticks. Compare your answer with another group before consulting the teacher key.<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-30\">AI claim audit and design challenge<\/h3><p>[AI CLASSROOM — CONTRASTING CLAIMS] A: “A high R² proves the beam model is correct, so the estimated modulus applies to the entire tree species.” B: “The measured force–displacement relationship was approximately linear over the tested range. Geometry and conditioning uncertainty limit interpretation of the apparent modulus.”<\/p><p>For each claim identify evidence required, assumptions, unsupported wording and a corrected conclusion. Verify at least one technical point against a credible mechanics source.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-31\">Optional approved AI interaction<\/h4><p>[AI OPTIONAL] Prompt: Critique this anonymised experimental method for confounding, pseudoreplication and unjustified model assumptions. Do not invent data or references. Distinguish suggestions from verified claims. Record the prompt, tool/model name where known, date, relevant output and your acceptance or rejection of each suggestion. Non-AI alternative: audit with the model handout and peer checklist.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-32\">Design challenge<\/h4><p>Recommend specimens for members of a small model bridge at the tutor-specified span. Compare measured stiffness, mass and uncertainty. State where evidence is insufficient, including joints, failure, repeated loading and whole-structure behaviour. Provide a labelled sketch on a separate sheet.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-33\">Peer review<\/h4><p>Does the recommendation cite numerical results? Are assumptions explicit? Are technical repeats separated from specimens? Does the report avoid treating apparent modulus as verified material truth? Identify one strength, one required correction and one useful further experiment.<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-34\">5 Assessment brief and marking rubric<\/h3><p>Individual report: 1,500 words excluding references, tables and appendices. Suggested weighting: 90% of the unit assessment. Include a reproducible method, traceable group-data provenance, SI calculations, individual analysis, uncertainty, model critique, design recommendation and AI-use disclosure. Submit raw data and transparent formulas or code. Follow local rules on permitted assistance.<\/p><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:570px\"><table><tr><th>Report criterion<\/th><th>Weight<\/th><th>Strong first year evidence<\/th><\/tr><tr><td>Question and physical reasoning<\/td><td>15%<\/td><td>Testable question; distinguishes geometry, stiffness, modulus and strength; relevant assumptions.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Design and reproducibility<\/td><td>20%<\/td><td>Justified sampling, controls, repeat structure and approved procedure; deviations documented.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Data analysis<\/td><td>25%<\/td><td>Traceable data, correct SI calculations, clear graphs, justified fit and residual inspection.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Uncertainty and critical evaluation<\/td><td>25%<\/td><td>Separates measurement, sampling and model limitations; claims remain proportionate.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Communication and integrity<\/td><td>15%<\/td><td>Coherent report, credible references, transparent contributions and AI disclosure.<\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><\/div><p>Indicative descriptors: strong work is accurate, justified and critically qualified; competent work is largely correct with some incomplete justification; developing work has limited analysis or significant omissions; insufficient work lacks interpretable evidence or has unresolved major errors. Apply the institution’s marking scale and academic-integrity process rather than inventing grade boundaries.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-35\">Individual oral check<\/h4><p>Suggested weighting: 10%. Ask students to explain one calculation, defend one design decision and identify a limitation that changes interpretation. Score physical reasoning, interpretation of their own data and critical judgement equally. Use an accessible equivalent where required by approved adjustments.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-36\">Formative diagnostic questions<\/h4><p>Convert 0.40 mm to metres. What are the units of a force–deflection slope?<\/p><p>Why do ten cycles on one stick not provide ten independent specimens?<\/p><p>Can stiffness or a high R² establish breaking strength? Explain.<\/p><p>Which uncertainty term is amplified by the fourth-power diameter dependence?<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-37\">Teacher answers and moderation notes<\/h3><h4 id=\"heading-38\">Simulated example<\/h4><p>k = 5 N/mm = 5,000 N/m. I = π(0.0060)⁴/64 ≈ 6.36 × 10⁻¹¹ m⁴. E_app = 5,000(0.200)³/(48I) ≈ 1.31 × 10¹⁰ Pa = 13.1 GPa. The exact straight line is constructed; it supplies no empirical estimate of noise, repeatability or population variability. Do not use it to claim experimental validation.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-39\">Diagnostic and activity answers<\/h4><p>0.40 mm = 0.00040 m. Slope of F against δ is N/m when SI units are used. Repeated cycles describe one specimen’s response and may be affected by loading history; independent specimens are needed to assess between-specimen variation. High R² measures fit to the chosen relationship, not truth of its assumptions or strength. Diameter uncertainty enters the approximate relative modulus uncertainty with coefficient 4.<\/p><p>Ideal-model scaling: doubling span increases displacement eightfold at constant F, E and I; doubling circular diameter reduces displacement sixteenfold at constant F, E and L. Real specimens may violate geometry, small-deflection, support or material assumptions.<\/p><p>Protocol audit: changed span, inadequate independent sampling, pseudoreplication, uncertain geometry/material matching, missing measurement controls and an unsupported stiffness-to-strength conclusion. Reward reasoned corrections, not just identification of labels. Claim B is more defensible, but still needs numerical results, fit diagnostics and explicit limits.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-40\">Marking and feedback<\/h4><p>Moderate a sample of reports using shared criteria. Accept inconclusive results when analysis is sound. Distinguish a calculation error from a conceptual error and avoid penalising the same fault repeatedly. Refer integrity concerns to institutional procedures; do not treat an AI detector score as proof. Give feedback on a specific reasoning or method improvement.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-41\">Sources for verification<\/h4><p>University of Cambridge. The Three Point Bend Test. https://mi.eng.cam.ac.uk/IALego/bender_files/bend_theory.pdf<\/p><p>Students should add sources appropriate to wood structure, conditioning or uncertainty when used in their discussion. Verify bibliographic details against the source itself; do not accept invented AI citations.<\/p><h3 id=\"heading-42\">6 Teaching evaluation and future application<\/h3><h4 id=\"heading-43\">Teaching process analysis<\/h4><p>The revised unit shifts from school-level description to first-year quantitative modelling. Characterisation precedes protocol design; piloting precedes data collection; analysis precedes application. This sequencing exposes the dependence of conclusions on measurement, sampling and physical assumptions. The extended two-hour sessions provide time for apparatus checks, independent thinking and critique, but actual timing must be trialled.<\/p><p>Scaffolded calculations and open analysis routes accommodate varied preparation without lowering the outcomes. Group practical work supports shared equipment use; individual reports and oral checks provide evidence of personal understanding. Practical access and mathematical confidence should be reviewed after each session, with scaffolds adjusted in response.<\/p><h4 id=\"heading-44\">Tool and model evaluation<\/h4><p>Generative AI supports drafting, alternative explanations and critique examples. It does not validate theory, references, student achievement or safe load limits. A spreadsheet or notebook makes numerical analysis inspectable; a tutor-verified worked example checks the workflow. No controlled comparison of AI models, preparation-time study or classroom outcome evaluation has been conducted. Any effectiveness claim remains provisional.<\/p><div class=\"scroll\"><div class=\"readable-table-scroll\" tabindex=\"0\" style=\"--table-readable-width:570px\"><table><tr><th>Stage<\/th><th>Action<\/th><th>Evidence to collect<\/th><\/tr><tr><td>Before delivery<\/td><td>Align to approved module outcomes; pilot apparatus and workload; review accessibility and AI rules.<\/td><td>Approved materials and feasible protocol.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>During delivery<\/td><td>Check concepts, participation, raw-data quality and analysis decisions.<\/td><td>Diagnostic responses, logs, timings and formative work.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>After delivery<\/td><td>Moderate reports and review feedback against each outcome.<\/td><td>Criterion patterns and specific misconceptions.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Next iteration<\/td><td>Revise weak instructions, data templates and support; compare cautiously across cohorts.<\/td><td>Documented revisions and evidence of changed understanding.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Future applications<\/td><td>Extend to manufactured dowels, paper beams or conditioned wood with fresh risk and model checks.<\/td><td>A new protocol suited to the material and question.<\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><\/div><p>[AI REVIEW] Use anonymised misconception summaries to prepare practice tasks. Two deliberately different learning experiences.<\/h2><p>The purpose is to show how I turn a shared subject into learning that suits different starting points, rather than merely changing the wording. Investigating sticks provides an accessible practical context. The school pathway develops observation, measurement, fair testing and evidence-based explanation. The university pathway adds quantitative modelling, uncertainty, independent analysis and criticism of assumptions.<\/p><h3>The learning design process<\/h3><p>I began with the audience, likely prior knowledge, intended outcomes and practical constraints. I then aligned each outcome with an activity and observable evidence of understanding. The sequence moves from examining specimens to planning, investigation, interpretation and application. Support is adjusted through diagnostic questions and formative checks; age alone does not determine a learner’s needs.<\/p><h3>Assessment and feedback<\/h3><p>Group practical work supports discussion and shared equipment, while individual explanations provide evidence of personal understanding. Neither a polished interface nor a correct objective answer proves learning effectiveness. Evaluation should examine individual reasoning, accessibility, practical performance and transfer to a new problem.<\/p><h3>Learning design, curriculum and access<\/h3><p>I selected a familiar, low-cost material to make the intellectual task accessible without making the reasoning trivial. The curriculum emphasis is scientific enquiry: distinguishing a measurement from an inference, a fair comparison from a causal claim, and stiffness from breaking strength. Local subject specifications must be checked before treating these examples as a mapped unit.<\/p><p>I use a diagnostic starting point, a worked example, guided practice and an independent explanation. The support can be increased or faded in response to evidence; age does not prescribe ability. The outcome is a defensible investigation and recommendation, supported by measurements.<\/p><p><strong>Sequence and support:<\/strong> four 60-minute lessons move through Observe and compare → Predict and plan → Investigate and analyse → Evaluate and apply. Teacher modelling, worked examples, vocabulary, recording templates and sentence starters make the reasoning visible. Support is reduced or extended in response to evidence, rather than fixed ability labels.<\/p><p><strong>Why this approach:<\/strong> learners practise measurement before interpreting results, and plans must be approved before practical work. Group roles provide access and participation; individual conclusions reveal understanding beyond the group. \"<h2>中文教学指南：十五岁学生<\/h2><p><strong>简明翻译版。<\/strong>本版介绍主要课程顺序、概念和评估，并非下方完整英语工作表及评分描述的逐项翻译。<\/p><h3>目标与成果<\/h3><p>探究树枝特征与其表现之间的关系。学生应能描述至少四项特征；使用适当单位测量长度、直径和质量；提出可检验假设；识别变量；实施教师批准的探究；作图；说明两项局限及相应改进。暂以英格兰第四关键阶段科学探究要求为参考，实施时须对照本校实际课程。<\/p><h3>准备与安全<\/h3><p>准备已编号和检查的试样、尺、天平、可用的卡尺、稳定支架及记录表。剔除尖锐、开裂起刺或发霉试样。教师须预先测试跨距和小载荷，使弯曲可测且不造成损坏。不得以折断为目标。手和脸应远离试验区；发现开裂声、滑动或永久变形时立即停止。使用预先收集的材料，避免破坏栖息地。<\/p><h3>第一课：观察与比较，六十分钟<\/h3><p>0–8分钟：描述两根树枝并预测表现。8–16分钟：区分观察与推断，介绍词汇。16–25分钟：示范测量、单位和精度。25–45分钟：检查至少四个试样，轮换测量、记录、器材和核查角色。45–55分钟：比较结果并提出可检验问题。55–60分钟：提交一项观察、一项推断及一项带单位的测量。<\/p><h3>第二课：预测与计划，六十分钟<\/h3><p>核心问题：固定载荷下，直径与弯曲有何关系？将位移定义为中点相对无载位置的垂直移动。确定编号、直径测量位置、跨距、总载荷、加载位置、试样方向、读数时间及重复次数。互评后获得教师批准。树种、含水量、节疤和状态可能混杂比较。重复读取同一试样不等于增加独立试样。<\/p><h3>第三课：探究与分析，六十分钟<\/h3><p>按批准方案记录加载与无载读数并求差。卸载后检查是否恢复，再重复。保持约定条件一致。对有效读数求平均，以直径为横轴、平均位移为纵轴绘制散点图，标注单位并采用均匀刻度。不要按试样顺序连点，也不要仅因结果不符合预测而删除它。若时间不足，应先试行工作量，再减少样本或另设作图时间。<\/p><h3>第四课：评价与应用，六十分钟<\/h3><p>判断证据是否支持假设，引用至少两项结果，说明两项局限及各自改进。为教师指定跨距的小型模型桥构件推荐试样，附示意图，并提出接头、结构布局、重复加载和破坏强度等后续试验。推荐不等于已证明承载能力或桥梁安全。<\/p><h3>核心工作表<\/h3><p>观察记录：试样、长度、直径、质量、纹理、状态和观察。计划：问题、假设、比较变量、测量结果、控制条件、方法、无法控制的因素、停止条件和批准。结果表：试样、直径（毫米）、三次位移（毫米）及平均值；另记跨距、总载荷和读数时间。<\/p><p>平均值＝有效位移读数之和÷有效次数。仅作模拟示例：(4＋5＋3)÷3＝4毫米。不能把模拟数字当作实验结果。在可比条件下弯曲较少，说明该装置下抗弯更强，并不证明断裂载荷更高。<\/p><h3>推理活动<\/h3><p>将陈述分为观察、推断和预测。例如“天平显示24克”是观察；“它可能含水更多”是推断；“相同载荷下它会弯曲更少”是预测。审查一个对粗细树枝使用不同跨距和载荷的错误计划，修正控制条件、读数次数和抽样，并纠正“弯曲最少就总是最结实”的结论。<\/p><h3>评估与答案<\/h3><p>个人成果应包括问题与假设、方法和变量、结果表与图、引用数据的结论、两项局限及改进、以及有依据的建议。可以共享小组数据，但解释必须独立。等效录音展示应保持相同科学要求。<\/p><p>另设十分知识检查：测量结果与单位2分；两个控制条件2分；3、4、5毫米平均值1分；重复与独立试样的区别2分；弯曲与破坏的区别1分；局限及相应改进2分。答案要点：中点垂直位移，毫米等长度单位；跨距和总载荷等控制条件；平均4毫米；重复反映一致性，独立试样反映试样间差异；未测断裂载荷。<\/p><p>探究量规共十五分，五个标准各0–3分：观察与测量、计划、分析、结论与应用、评价。0分表示无相关证据；1分为不完整或不一致；2分为清楚且大体正确；3分为准确、有论证且明确局限，具体以原始描述为准。十五分探究与十分检查分开报告，不能把总分当作经验证的GCSE等级界线。<\/p><h3>支持、人工智能与教学评价<\/h3><p>提供图示词汇、例题、引导表格、建议坐标刻度及适当口头回答方式。拓展可涉及仪器分辨率、变异和控制混杂因素的更强设计。教师可用人工智能起草资料和明确标注的错误示例，但必须核查；学生无需人工智能账户。不要上传可识别个人的作业。实施后查看起始与结束回答、作品、参与、时间和无障碍表现。目前尚未测得学习成效或备课时间节省。<\/p>\", \"<h2>中文教学指南：大学一年级<\/h2><p><strong>简明翻译版。<\/strong>保留核心概念、课程顺序、数值示例和评估标准。下方保留完整英语原版。<\/p><h3>目标与准备<\/h3><p>通过力—位移测量、分析和有限推断，探究树枝作为天然结构材料的表现。假定具备基础代数、国际单位制和作图能力；专门理论在课程中介绍。安排四次两小时课程，另加约六小时自主学习。先检查单位换算、斜率及刚度与破坏强度的区别。试验前，教师必须批准装置、步骤、载荷限制和停止条件。<\/p><h3>模型与局限<\/h3><p>理想中央加载三点弯曲模型：δ＝FL³/(48EI)；k＝dF/dδ；圆截面I＝πd⁴/64；E_app＝kL³/(48I)。区分试样及装置刚度k、材料模量E、抗弯刚度EI和破坏强度。E_app依赖几何、支承、材料和小变形假设；条件不足时仅报告k。锥度、椭圆截面、各向异性、含水量和节疤不能简单当作随机测量噪声。<\/p><h3>第一次课程：表征与理论<\/h3><p>0–15分钟诊断；15–35分钟介绍模型及SI计算；35–70分钟编号并记录质量、长度，以及三个位置各两个垂直方向直径、状态和方向；70–85分钟休息并整理几何；85–105分钟比较试样和假设，区分测量不确定度与生物变异；105–120分钟批判“越粗总是越强”，提交问题和抽样理由。<\/p><h3>第二次课程：方案与试验<\/h3><p>0–15分钟复核假设；15–35分钟审查缺陷方案；35–60分钟设计固定跨距的加载卸载、读数时间和可追溯记录；60–70分钟休息及教师审核；70–100分钟在批准范围内试验，检查分辨率、重复性及恢复；100–120分钟修订方案、分析与排除标准。明确控制条件、独立试样和技术重复。同一试样十个循环不等于十个独立试样。<\/p><h3>第三次课程：测量与分析<\/h3><p>0–10分钟确认设备与限制；10–50分钟采集独立试样数据并适当重复；50–60分钟检查数据完整性；60–85分钟用SI绘制F对δ图，对合理线性范围进行含截距拟合，检查残差及加载卸载差异；85–105分钟估计k及有依据的E_app，分开讨论测量敏感性和试样差异；105–120分钟互评并写有限结论。不得无理由强制零截距，不应隐藏滞回、漂移或残余变形。<\/p><h3>第四次课程：批判与应用<\/h3><p>0–20分钟展示图及局限；20–40分钟核查对照结论的证据与假设；40–65分钟结合刚度、质量和不确定度推荐模型桥构件；65–75分钟休息并准备报告结构；75–100分钟互评；100–115分钟个人口头检查或获批等效形式；115–120分钟提交修改重点和人工智能声明。不能由本试验推断整桥安全或断裂载荷。<\/p><h3>记录与模拟算例<\/h3><p>保留试样和循环编号、添加质量、力、位移、加载或卸载及时间。另记仪器分辨率、零点、附件质量、方向、偏离方案和修正。保留原始数据并说明小组贡献。<\/p><p>单个理想试样的模拟数据：力为0、1、2、3、4牛，位移为0、0.20、0.40、0.60、0.80毫米。L＝0.200米，d＝0.0060米。结果：k＝5牛/毫米＝5000牛/米；I≈6.36×10⁻¹¹米⁴；E_app≈1.31×10¹⁰帕＝13.1吉帕。这些是构造数据，不是实验观察或独立重复。完美直线不能估计真实噪声，也不能验证物理模型。<\/p><h3>不确定度与批判判断<\/h3><p>在圆截面模型、小且相互独立的标准不确定度条件下：u(E)/E≈√[(u(k)/k)²＋(3u(L)/L)²＋(4u(d)/d)²]。直径2%的不确定度单独贡献约8%的模量相对不确定度。此传播式不包含模型偏差、锥度、各向异性或未知含水量。高R²不能验证物理假设，也不能证明破坏强度。<\/p><p>理想模型中，其他量不变时跨距加倍使位移增至八倍；圆直径加倍使位移降至十六分之一。应解释真实树枝何时不满足这些预测。审查改变控制条件、独立抽样不足、伪重复和无依据推断。<\/p><h3>评估<\/h3><p>个人报告1500字，不含参考文献、表格和附录，建议占单元90%。报告内标准：问题与物理推理15%；设计与可重复性20%；数据分析25%；不确定度与批判评价25%；沟通与诚信15%。提交原始数据、可检查公式或代码、共享数据来源及帮助声明。口头检查建议占10%：解释一个计算、论证一个决策、指出一个改变解释的局限；物理推理、数据解释和批判判断等权。须采用本校评分尺度与规定。<\/p><h3>支持、人工智能与修订<\/h3><p>提供引导电子表格、换算例题和模板，同时提供开放分析路径。拓展关注几何敏感性、不确定度传播或不同模型。因无法实践而使用模拟数据时，实践能力仍需另行取证。
